title: 14 Penn Plaza LLC v. Pyett
summary: The Court decided that when a union contract clearly and unmistakably requires age discrimination claims under the ADEA to be arbitrated, employees covered by that contract cannot bring those claims in court.

title: Abbate v. United States
summary: The Court held that the Fifth Amendment's Double Jeopardy Clause did not bar a federal prosecution for a conspiracy that had already resulted in a state court conviction under state law.

title: Abbott v. United States
summary: The Court ruled that the five-year minimum sentence under 18 U.S.C. § 924(c) for using or possessing a deadly weapon in drug trafficking or violent crimes was added to any other mandatory sentence, including for the underlying offense.

title: Adams v. Williams
summary: The Court held that a tip from a known informant can create enough reasonable suspicion to justify a patdown under Terry v. Ohio.

title: Aetna Life Insurance Co. v. Lavoie
Agostini v. Felton
summary: The Court overruled its earlier decision and held that it did not violate the Establishment Clause for a state-sponsored education program to let public school teachers instruct at religious schools, if the material was secular and neutral and no excessive entanglement existed.

title: Aguilar v. Felton
summary: The Court held that New York City's program sending public school teachers into parochial schools to provide remedial education to disadvantaged children under Title I caused excessive church-state entanglement and violated the Establishment Clause.

title: Aguilar v. Texas
summary: The Court held that a search warrant affidavit may rest on hearsay, but the magistrate must be told the underlying circumstances relied on by the informant and those supporting the conclusion that the undisclosed informant was credible or reliable.

title: Air & Liquid Systems Corp. v. DeVries
summary: The Court held that, in maritime tort cases, a manufacturer has a duty to warn when its product requires incorporation of a part, it knows or has reason to know the integrated product is likely dangerous, and it has no reason to believe users will realize the danger.

title: Alabama Legislative Black Caucus v. Alabama
summary: The Court overturned a federal district court decision that had upheld Alabama's 2012 redrawing of its electoral districts.

title: Albemarle Paper Co. v. Moody
summary: In a Title VII employment discrimination case, the Court held that disparate impact plaintiffs did not need to prove bad faith to be entitled to backpay, and it expanded on the requirement that employment tests be job-related.

title: Albertson v. Subversive Activities Control Board
summary: The Court ruled that people believed to be Communist Party members could not be required to register with the Subversive Activities Control Board, because the required information could be used to prosecute them and so violated their Fifth Amendment self-incrimination rights.

title: Alexander v. South Carolina State Conference of the NAACP
summary: In a challenge to South Carolina's 1st congressional district map as a racial gerrymander, the Court held the district court's finding that race predominated was not sufficiently supported by evidence, reversed it as clear error, and remanded.

title: Ali v. Federal Bureau of Prisons
Alice Corp. v. CLS Bank International
Allied Structural Steel Co. v. Spannaus
Alvarez v. Smith
summary: In a case about the Chicago Police Department's seizure of property, the Court declared the case moot because the parties agreed there was no longer any contention over the seized property.

title: American Communications Ass'n v. Douds
summary: The Court held that the Taft–Hartley Act's anti-communist oath requirement for labor union leaders did not violate the First Amendment, was not an ex post facto law or bill of attainder, and was not a prohibited test oath.

title: American Express Co. v. Italian Colors Restaurant
American Legion v. American Humanist Association
summary: The Court reversed the Fourth Circuit, ruling that a World War I memorial in the shape of a Latin cross on government-owned land did not violate the Establishment Clause since it had stood for decades without controversy.

title: American Needle, Inc. v. National Football League
Americans for Prosperity Foundation v. Bonta
summary: The Court ruled that California's requirement that non-profits disclose their donors' identities to the Attorney General before soliciting donations burdened donors' First Amendment rights, was not narrowly tailored, and was invalid.

title: Anders v. California
summary: When a court-appointed attorney sought to withdraw from a criminal appeal as frivolous, the Court ruled that the motion must come with a brief outlining possible grounds, the appellate court must independently review the case, and the defendant may appeal pro se or with other counsel.

title: Anderson's-Black Rock, Inc. v. Pavement Salvage Co.
Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, Inc. v. Goldsmith
summary: The Court ruled that a foundation's licensing of Andy Warhol's Prince Series images, based on a photographer's photograph of Prince, was not protected by fair use, as the works shared a similar purpose.

title: Animal Science Products v. Hebei Welcome Pharmaceuticals
summary: In a price-fixing suit where a Chinese company claimed Chinese law required its conduct, the Court unanimously reversed the Second Circuit, holding that a foreign government's statements about its law get respectful consideration but not conclusive effect.

title: Antoine v. Washington
summary: The Court held that treaties and laws must be construed in favor of Native Americans, that the Supremacy Clause barred applying state game laws to the tribe, and that Congress showed no intent to subject the tribe to state hunting jurisdiction.

title: Anza v. Ideal Steel Supply Corp.
summary: In a dispute over standing under the civil RICO provision, the Court held that a plaintiff must show he or she was the direct victim of the defendant's RICO violation, so a business could not sue a competitor that gained an advantage by not paying taxes.

title: Apodaca v. Oregon
summary: The Court held that state juries may convict a defendant of a felony by a less-than-unanimous verdict, affirming the Oregon Court of Appeals and finding Oregon's practice did not violate the Sixth Amendment right to trial by jury.

title: Apple Inc. v. Pepper
summary: In a dispute over whether consumers could bring antitrust claims over Apple's App Store practices, the Court ruled that because consumers bought apps directly from Apple, they had standing under Illinois Brick to sue.

title: Apprendi v. New Jersey
summary: In a case about aggravating factors in crimes, the Court ruled that the Sixth Amendment jury trial right prohibited judges from enhancing sentences beyond statutory maxima based on facts not decided by a jury beyond a reasonable doubt.

title: Arbaugh v. Y & H Corp.
summary: In a Title VII employment discrimination case, the Court ruled that the fifteen-employee numerosity requirement was not a limit on courts' jurisdiction but a substantive element of the claim, which a defendant must raise before verdict or waive.

title: Arizona Christian School Tuition Organization v. Winn
summary: The case concerned Arizona taxpayers who challenged a state tax credit for donations to school tuition organizations funding private or religious schools, and the Court ruled that the taxpayers lacked standing to sue.

title: Arizona Free Enterprise Club's Freedom Club PAC v. Bennett
Arizona v. City and County of San Francisco
summary: In a case about the ability of states to defend federal regulations in court, the Court did not resolve the questions presented and instead dismissed review as improvidently granted.

title: Arizona v. Fulminante
summary: The Court, in a case about the standard of review for an allegedly coerced confession, ruled the confession involuntary, held that the harmless error rule applied, and found its use as evidence was not harmless.

title: Arizona v. Gant
summary: The Court held that the Fourth Amendment requires officers to show an actual and continuing threat to their safety from an arrestee, or a need to preserve evidence of the crime of arrest, to justify a warrantless vehicle search incident to arrest after occupants are secured.

title: Arizona v. Maricopa County Medical Society
summary: The Court rejected a doctors' society's defense that its maximum-fee arrangement for patients under certain health insurance plans was necessary and beneficial, finding the price fixing was not truly necessary and the justifications failed.

title: Arkansas v. Texas
summary: In a suit by Arkansas against Texas over a foundation's contract with the University of Arkansas, the Court held that the suit was between two states and that the Foundation was not an indispensable party.

title: Arlington Central School District Board of Education v. Murphy
summary: In a case about experts' fees under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act, the Court ruled that the Act does not authorize payment of the prevailing parents' experts' fees.

title: Aro Manufacturing Co. v. Convertible Top Replacement Co.
Arrowsmith v. Commissioner
summary: The Court considered whether taxpayers' payment of a judgment against a corporation they had earlier liquidated was an ordinary business loss, and held it was a capital loss, agreeing with the Second Circuit.

title: Asahi Metal Industry Co. v. Superior Court
Ashcroft v. American Civil Liberties Union
summary: The Court ruled that the Child Online Protection Act was unconstitutional because it violated the First Amendment's guarantee of freedom of speech.

title: Ashcroft v. Free Speech Coalition
summary: The Court struck down two overbroad provisions of the Child Pornography Prevention Act of 1996 because they abridged the freedom to engage in a substantial amount of lawful speech, rejecting a bid to widen categorically unprotected speech.

title: Atlantic Marine Construction Co. v. United States District Court
Atlas Roofing Co. v. Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission
summary: The Court held that the Seventh Amendment did not require a jury trial to enforce civil penalties for violating a federal "public rights" statute, so an administrative agency could enforce them.

title: Auer v. Robbins
summary: In a dispute over whether St. Louis police sergeants and lieutenants were owed overtime under the Fair Labor Standards Act, the Court held that it should defer to the Secretary of Labor's interpretation of the regulations.

title: Ayers v. Belmontes
summary: The Court held that a catch-all jury instruction allowing consideration of any circumstance extenuating the gravity of the crime permitted jurors to consider post-crime evidence and was consistent with the right to present mitigating evidence in death-penalty sentencing.

title: Ayotte v. Planned Parenthood of Northern New England
summary: In a facial challenge to a state parental notification abortion law, the Court vacated the First Circuit's judgment and remanded, holding only on remedy that invalidating a statute entirely is not always necessary because lower courts may render narrower relief.

title: Babb v. Wilkie
summary: The Court ruled that federal employees suing under the Age Discrimination in Employment Act only had to prove age was a motivating factor to sue, though but-for causation was still needed to determine the appropriate remedy.

title: Babbitt v. Youpee
summary: The Court held that a provision escheating to the tribe, upon the owner's death, small fractional interests in an allotment (under two percent and earning less than $100 in five years) worked an unconstitutional taking.

title: Bailey v. United States
summary: The Court interpreted a federal statute imposing a mandatory five-year term for "using" a firearm in a drug trafficking crime, ruling that "use" means "active employment" of a firearm, not mere possession, and remanded the cases.

title: Baldwin v. New York
summary: The Court ruled that defendants have a Sixth Amendment right to a jury trial for offenses punishable by imprisonment for more than six months.

title: Bank of America National Trust & Savings Ass'n v. 203 North LaSalle Street Partnership
Bank of America, N.A. v. Caulkett
summary: In a bankruptcy case, the Court held that a Chapter 7 debtor could not void a junior mortgage under 11 U.S.C. § 506(d) when the senior mortgage debt exceeded the property's current market value.

title: BankAmerica Corp. v. United States
summary: In an antitrust case the U.S. government brought under Section 8 of the Clayton Act against banks and their holding companies over shared board members, the Court reversed the Ninth Circuit.

title: Barefoot v. Estelle
summary: In a death penalty case where the defendant argued psychiatrists could not accurately predict future dangerousness, the Court ruled that such psychiatric predictions could be presented to a jury during the sentencing phase of a capital trial.

title: Barnes v. Felix
summary: The Court, in a unanimous decision, reaffirmed the "totality of the circumstances" test for Fourth Amendment excessive force claims and rejected the "moment of the threat" test used by some Circuit Courts as excessively narrow.

title: Barnes v. Glen Theatre, Inc.
summary: The Court ruled that a state has the constitutional authority to ban public nudity, even as part of expressive conduct such as dancing, because doing so furthers a substantial government interest in protecting morality and order.

title: Barr v. Matteo
summary: The Court held that a federal executive official who issues a press release about their official duties is absolutely immune from libel suits, so the acting director could not be sued over his press release about two former employees.

title: Bartkus v. Illinois
summary: The Court held that coordination between federal and state officials did not implicate double jeopardy, and that a defendant acquitted of a federal crime could be convicted of a state crime on the same evidence without violating due process.

title: Barton v. Barr
summary: The Court upheld an Eleventh Circuit decision that permanent residents rendered inadmissible for certain crimes committed within their first seven years of continuous residence were ineligible for cancellation of removal.

title: Bates v. City of Little Rock
summary: The Court held that the First Amendment forbade state governments from compelling disclosure of an organization's membership lists through a tax-exemption regulatory scheme.

title: Bearden v. Georgia
summary: The Court held that a local government could imprison or jail someone for not paying a fine only if a hearing showed that the person could have paid it but willfully chose not to.

title: Beck v. Ohio
summary: The Court reversed the Ohio Supreme Court, holding that the record did not show probable cause for a warrantless arrest, so evidence found in the search incident to that arrest was inadmissible and the conviction was vacated.

title: Beckles v. United States
summary: The Court considered whether the residual clause in the advisory Sentencing Guidelines was unconstitutionally vague, and it unanimously affirmed the lower court, holding the advisory Guidelines are not subject to vagueness challenges under the Due Process Clause.

title: Bell v. Maryland
summary: The Court, in a case over criminal trespass convictions of twelve African American students at a private restaurant, vacated the Maryland Court of Appeals' judgment and remanded because the state law had changed.

title: Bell v. Wolfish
summary: The Court considered the constitutionality of conditions of confinement in federal short-term detention facilities and found that, although pre-trial detainees' treatment is constrained by the Constitution, all the challenged policies passed constitutional scrutiny.

title: Bellotti v. Baird (1976)
summary: The Court unanimously upheld a Massachusetts law requiring parental consent to a minor's abortion, where a judge could order consent for good cause if one or both parents refused.

title: Benton v. Maryland
summary: In a double jeopardy case, the Court ruled that the Fifth Amendment's Double Jeopardy Clause applies to the states, and in doing so expressly overruled Palko v. Connecticut.

title: Berger v. North Carolina State Conference of the NAACP
Berghuis v. Smith
summary: The Court ruled that a Michigan jury selection system resulting in low representation of African Americans in Kent County did not violate the Sixth Amendment, because the statistical disparity did not satisfy the Duren test.

title: Besser Manufacturing Co. v. United States
summary: The Court upheld a ruling that the dominant concrete block-making machine manufacturer violated antitrust laws through acquisitions, patent abuses and licensing vetoes, and approved compulsory reasonable-royalty licensing of its patents and compulsory sales of machines.

title: Biden v. Texas
summary: In a suit by Texas and Missouri over the termination of the "Remain in Mexico" policy, the Court reversed the lower courts and ruled that the Biden administration and DHS legally had the authority to end the program.

title: Bigelow v. Virginia
summary: The Court established First Amendment protection for commercial speech in a challenge to government regulation of advertising, determining that such publications qualify as speech under the First Amendment.

title: Bivens v. Six Unknown Named Agents
summary: The Court ruled that an implied cause of action existed for an individual whose Fourth Amendment protection against unreasonable searches and seizures had been violated by the Federal Bureau of Narcotics.

title: Blanton v. City of North Las Vegas
BMW of North America, Inc. v. Gore
BNSF Railway Co. v. Tyrrell
summary: The Court held that Montana courts lacked personal jurisdiction over a railroad that was neither incorporated nor headquartered in Montana, even though it had over 2,000 miles of track and 2,000 employees there.

title: Board of Education of Kiryas Joel Village School District v. Grumet
Board of Education of Oklahoma City v. Dowell
Board of Regents of State Colleges v. Roth
summary: In a case over a nontenured state university teacher not being rehired without a hearing, the Court held that the Fourteenth Amendment did not require a hearing before nonrenewal unless the teacher showed a deprivation of a liberty or property interest.

title: Bond v. United States (2014)
summary: The Court found that a woman's attack on her friend using dangerous toxicants was not use of a chemical weapon under section 229(a)(1) of the Chemical Weapons Convention Implementation Act.

title: Borden Ranch Partnership v. Army Corps of Engineers
Boumediene v. Bush
summary: The Court, in a case brought by a Guantanamo detainee, held that the detainees had a constitutional right to habeas corpus and that the Military Commissions Act of 2006 was an unconstitutional suspension of that right.

title: Bowers v. Hardwick
summary: The Court upheld the constitutionality of a Georgia sodomy law criminalizing oral and anal sex in private between consenting adults, reasoning that the Constitution did not confer a fundamental right to engage in homosexual sodomy.

title: Bowsher v. Synar
summary: The Court struck down the Gramm–Rudman–Hollings Act as an unconstitutional usurpation of executive power by Congress, because the law empowered Congress to terminate the Comptroller General for specified reasons.

title: Boynton v. Virginia
summary: The Court overturned the trespassing conviction of an African American law student who sat in a "whites only" bus terminal restaurant, holding that racial segregation in public transportation violated the Interstate Commerce Act.

title: BP America Production Co. v. Burton
summary: The Court unanimously ruled that a statute of limitations on government actions for contract claims did not apply to a federal administrative agency's actions to recover royalties on federal oil and gas leases.

title: BP p.l.c. v. Mayor and City Council of Baltimore
Braden v. 30th Judicial Circuit Court of Kentucky
Brady v. Maryland
summary: The Court held that under the Due Process Clause, the prosecution must turn over to a criminal defendant any significant evidence in its possession that suggests the defendant is not guilty.

title: Brandenburg v. Ohio
summary: The Court held that the government cannot punish inflammatory speech unless it is directed to inciting imminent lawless action and likely to produce it, and struck down Ohio's criminal syndicalism statute for broadly prohibiting mere advocacy of violence.

title: Brecht v. Abrahamson
summary: The Court held that federal courts deciding whether to grant habeas relief for unconstitutional trial error should assess such claims using the harmless error standard from Kotteakos v. United States.

title: Brinegar v. United States
summary: The Court, in a case about warrantless searches, held that police need not always be factually correct in conducting such a search, but the search must always be reasonable.

title: Brooke Group Ltd. v. Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp.
Buckeye Check Cashing, Inc. v. Cardegna
Bucklew v. Precythe
summary: In a challenge to a state's method of execution under the Eighth Amendment, the Court held that a death-sentenced convict claiming excessive pain must show that alternative methods exist and would clearly cause less pain than the state's method.

title: Buckley v. American Constitutional Law Foundation, Inc.
Buckley v. Valeo
summary: In a challenge to campaign finance limits under the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971, the Court held that limits on election expenditures were unconstitutional because they contravened the First Amendment's protection of free speech.

title: Buckman Co. v. Plaintiffs' Legal Committee
summary: The Court considered whether the federal FDCA pre-empted a state-law fraud-on-the-FDA claim, and it decided to reject the lawsuit attempt.

title: Bullcoming v. New Mexico
summary: The Court considered whether the Confrontation Clause allows a supervisor to testify about lab results transcribed by a non-testifying analyst, and held that a surrogate analyst could not testify about the certifying analyst's testimonial forensic report.

title: Burdick v. Takushi
summary: The Court held that Hawaii laws effectively prohibiting write-in voting did not violate the First or Fourteenth Amendment, reasoning that getting nominated under Hawaii's election laws was relatively easy.

title: Burks v. United States
summary: The Court held that when an appellate court reverses a conviction for insufficient evidence, the Double Jeopardy Clause bars a second prosecution, so the only just remedy is to order an acquittal rather than allow a new trial.

title: Burlington Northern & Santa Fe Railway Co. v. White
Burnham v. Superior Court of California
summary: The Court unanimously held that a state court may constitutionally exercise personal jurisdiction over a non-resident served with process while temporarily visiting the state, though the justices disagreed on the reasoning.

title: Burrage v. United States
summary: In a case about penalty enhancement under the Controlled Substances Act, the Court unanimously held that a defendant cannot be liable for the enhancement unless the drug use was a but-for cause of the death or injury, at least when it was not an independently sufficient cause.

title: Burwell v. Hobby Lobby Stores, Inc.
summary: The Court ruled that privately held for-profit corporations with religious objections could be exempt from the contraceptive mandate under the Religious Freedom Restoration Act, and struck down the mandate as applied to such companies.

title: Bush v. Gore
summary: In a dispute over a Florida statewide recount of undervotes in the 2000 presidential election, the Court held that no constitutional recount could be conducted in the remaining time, and that the recount violated the Equal Protection Clause.

title: Bush v. Palm Beach County Canvassing Board
Butler v. Michigan
summary: The Court held that laws criminalizing the sale of non-obscene literature to adults because of its perceived unsuitability for children were unconstitutional under the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

title: Butz v. Economou
summary: In a case about the legal immunity of federal officials sued on constitutional grounds, the Court held that they were entitled only to qualified immunity, except for duties where absolute immunity could be shown to be essential.

title: C&A Carbone, Inc. v. Town of Clarkstown
Calderon v. Thompson
summary: The Court held that a federal court of appeals has an inherent power to recall its mandate, but in habeas corpus cases that power may be exercised only in extraordinary circumstances, given the emphasis on finality of criminal judgments.

title: Califano v. Goldfarb
summary: The Court held that a Social Security provision requiring widowers, but not widows, to have received at least half their support from the deceased spouse was invidious discrimination against female wage earners and violated Fifth Amendment due process.

title: California Bankers Ass'n v. Shultz
summary: The Court held that the Bank Secrecy Act, which required banks to record transactions and report certain high-dollar domestic and foreign transactions to the Treasury, did not violate the First, Fourth, or Fifth Amendments.

title: California Retail Liquor Dealers Ass'n v. Midcal Aluminum, Inc.
California v. Acevedo
summary: The Court held that police may search an automobile and containers within it when they have probable cause to believe contraband or evidence is inside, and it overruled earlier precedents that required a warrant for containers alone.

title: California v. Green
summary: The Court held that the Sixth Amendment's Confrontation Clause did not bar admitting a witness's prior inconsistent statements when the witness testified at trial and faced full cross-examination, or prior preliminary hearing testimony given with adequate opportunity for cross-examination.

title: California v. Texas
summary: In a challenge to the Affordable Care Act's individual mandate after its tax penalty was reduced to zero, the Court ruled that Texas and the other challenging states lacked standing because they had shown no past or future injury from the provision.

title: Cameron v. EMW Women's Surgical Center, P.S.C.
Camreta v. Greene
summary: The Court held that government officials who won on qualified immunity grounds could still appeal the lower court's underlying ruling that their seizure of a schoolchild was unconstitutional.

title: Cantero v. Bank of America, N.A.
summary: In a dispute over whether New York's interest-on-escrow law was preempted as applied to national banks, the Court held that the Second Circuit failed to analyze preemption consistently with the Dodd-Frank Act and Barnett Bank.

title: Caperton v. A.T. Massey Coal Co.
summary: The Court held that the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment requires judges to recuse themselves not only for actual bias or an economic interest in the case, but also when "extreme facts" create a "probability of bias."

title: Carey v. Brown
summary: The Court found unjustified and unconstitutional an Illinois law that banned residential picketing but exempted labor disputes, because its distinction was based on the subject matter of a protest.

title: Carson v. Makin
summary: The Court ruled that Maine's restrictions barring school vouchers from paying tuition at religious private schools violated the Free Exercise Clause because they discriminated against religious schools and the parents who chose them.

title: Case v. Montana
summary: The Court addressed whether police may enter a home without a warrant under the emergency aid exception based on a reasonable belief someone needs help, and held that an objectively reasonable basis suffices, which the officers' entry satisfied.

title: Cedar Point Nursery v. Hassid
summary: The Court held that a California regulation requiring agricultural employers to let labor organizers regularly access their property for union recruitment was a per se taking under the Fifth Amendment, so it could not be enforced without just compensation.

title: Cedar Rapids Community School District v. Garret F.
summary: The Court ruled that the IDEA's related services provision required public school districts to fund continuous, one-on-one nursing care for disabled children, despite the school district's arguments about the cost of the services.

title: Cedric Kushner Promotions, Ltd. v. King
summary: The case concerned how far RICO reached certain corporation-individual organizations, and the Court unanimously decided to apply the Act to respondent Don King.

title: Celotex Corp. v. Catrett
summary: The Court held that a party moving for summary judgment need show only that the opposing party lacks evidence sufficient to support its case.

title: Central Bank of Denver, N.A. v. First Interstate Bank of Denver, N.A.
summary: In a securities fraud case, the Court held that private civil liability under Rule 10b-5 does not extend to aiders and abettors who do not themselves engage in a manipulative or deceptive practice, so private plaintiffs could not bring such suits.

title: Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp. v. Public Service Commission
Central Laborers' Pension Fund v. Heinz
Chatrie v. United States
summary: The Court held that a geofence warrant is a search subject to the Fourth Amendment, reaffirming and expanding its earlier holding on warrantless access to historical cell site location information.

title: Cheney v. United States District Court
Chevron USA Inc. v. Plaquemines Parish
Chiarella v. United States
summary: The Court held that a printer's employee who deduced the identities of takeover target companies and traded in their stock without disclosing his knowledge had not violated § 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 or SEC Rule 10b-5.

title: Chiles v. Salazar
summary: The Court ruled that the First Amendment requires strict scrutiny of state laws restricting what therapists may say to clients, reversing the lower courts' rulings upholding Colorado's ban on conversion therapy for minors and remanding the case.

title: Christiansburg Garment Co. v. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
Cipollone v. Liggett Group, Inc.
summary: In a suit by a smoker against tobacco companies, the Court held that the Surgeon General's warning did not preclude lawsuits by smokers against tobacco companies on the basis of several claims.

title: CITGO Asphalt Refining Co. v. Frescati Shipping Co.
summary: In a dispute over who bore the cleanup costs of a 2004 Delaware River oil spill, the Court ruled that the contract language required Citgo to provide a safe berth for the vessel, making Citgo ultimately responsible for the spill.

title: Citizens to Preserve Overton Park v. Volpe
City and County of San Francisco v. EPA
summary: The Court ruled in favor of San Francisco in a dispute over whether the Clean Water Act lets the EPA impose generic prohibitions in discharge permits that expose permit-holders to enforcement for violating water quality standards.

title: City News & Novelty, Inc. v. City of Waukesha
summary: The case concerned the denial of a business license for an adult store selling sexually explicit materials, and the Court dismissed it because the store had withdrawn its application to renew the license.

title: City of Cleburne v. Cleburne Living Center, Inc.
summary: The Court, applying rational basis review, struck down a city zoning ordinance as applied to a group home for intellectually disabled people, while declining to treat intellectually disabled people as a quasi-suspect or suspect class.

title: City of Los Angeles v. Alameda Books, Inc.
summary: In a challenge by two adult stores operating under one roof to a Los Angeles zoning ordinance restricting adult businesses, the Court ruled in favor of the city and reversed the lower court's decision.

title: City of Los Angeles v. Preferred Communications, Inc.
summary: The Court affirmed the Ninth Circuit and remanded, in a First Amendment dispute over restrictions on cable franchising, holding that the disputed factual issues needed fuller development before the legal issues could be decided.

title: City of New Orleans v. Dukes
Clark v. Martinez
summary: The Court ended the detention of people denied refugee status who were held in prison awaiting deportation even though they could not actually be deported because of a political stalemate with Cuba.

title: Clay v. Sun Insurance Office, Ltd.
Clay v. United States
summary: The Court unanimously reversed the conviction of Muhammad Ali for refusing military induction during the Vietnam War, finding the government had failed to properly specify why his conscientious objector application was denied.

title: Cleveland v. United States (2000)
summary: The Court held unanimously that, under the federal mail fraud statute, "property" did not include state video poker licences, because such transactions were not a vested right or expectation.

title: Clinton v. City of New York
summary: The Court held that the line-item veto under the Line Item Veto Act of 1996 violated the Presentment Clause, because it impermissibly let the president unilaterally amend or repeal parts of statutes duly passed by Congress.

title: Cohen v. Beneficial Industrial Loan Corp.
Cohen v. Cowles Media Co.
summary: The Court held that the First Amendment freedom of the press did not exempt journalists from generally applicable laws, in a case where newspapers published a source's name despite promising not to.

title: Coleman v. Thompson
summary: The Court held that a petitioner was barred from raising federal constitutional claims in federal habeas court because he had procedurally defaulted them in state habeas proceedings by filing his notice of appeal three days late.

title: College Savings Bank v. Florida Prepaid Postsecondary Education Expense Board
Collins v. Virginia
summary: In a Fourth Amendment search and seizure dispute over a warrantless search of a vehicle parked a few feet from a house, the Court ruled that the automobile exception does not apply to vehicles parked within a home or its curtilage.

title: Collins v. Yellen
summary: In a challenge to the structure of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, the Court ruled that restricting the President's removal of the FHFA director was unconstitutional, but dismissed shareholders' lawsuit because the takeover of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac was an established agency power.

title: Colorado River Water Conservation District v. United States
Commil USA, LLC v. Cisco Systems, Inc.
summary: The Court, in a case on the standard for induced patent infringement, held that induced infringement requires showing the defendant knew it was engaging in infringing conduct, and that a belief that the patent is invalid is not a defense.

title: Commodity Futures Trading Commission v. Schor
Communist Party v. Subversive Activities Control Board
summary: The Court upheld the constitutionality of a statute requiring organizations found to be controlled by the "world Communist movement" to register and disclose officers, funds, and membership, rejecting First and Fifth Amendment challenges.

title: Community for Creative Non-Violence v. Reid
Complete Auto Transit, Inc. v. Brady
Comptroller of the Treasury of Maryland v. Wynne
summary: The Court held that a state income-tax scheme taxing residents on in-state and out-of-state income violated the Dormant Commerce Clause when it did not give residents full credit for income taxes paid to other states.

title: Coney Island Auto Parts, Inc. v. Burton
summary: In a dispute over whether a party could move to set aside a default judgment as void after several years, the Court unanimously affirmed the Sixth Circuit's decision, which had denied the motion as untimely under Rule 60(c)(1).

title: Connecticut v. Doehr
summary: The Court held that a state statute allowing prejudgment attachment of a defendant's real property without prior notice or hearing, extraordinary circumstances, or a bond requirement violated the Fourteenth Amendment's Due Process Clause.

title: Connick v. Myers
summary: The Court reversed the lower courts' decision that had favored an assistant district attorney who was fired after circulating a questionnaire about management practices to her fellow prosecutors.

title: Connick v. Thompson
summary: In a case over a man's wrongful conviction after prosecutors suppressed exculpatory evidence, the Court reversed a $14 million jury award, holding a district attorney's office cannot be liable under Section 1983 for failure to train based on a single Brady violation.

title: Cooper Industries, Inc. v. Leatherman Tool Group, Inc.
Costco Wholesale Corp. v. Omega, S. A.
summary: In a copyright dispute over unauthorized sale of authentic, imported watches bearing a registered design, the court held that the first-sale doctrine was not a defense to claims of infringing distribution and importation.

title: County of Allegheny v. American Civil Liberties Union
summary: The Court considered holiday displays on public property in downtown Pittsburgh and held that the county violated the Establishment Clause by displaying a nativity scene in the courthouse, because its primary effect was to advance religion.

title: County of Maui v. Hawaii Wildlife Fund
summary: The Court ruled that under the Clean Water Act, pollutant discharges from a non-point source that reach navigable waters, such as through groundwater, require a permit when they are the "functional equivalent of a direct discharge."

title: Cox Communications, Inc. v. Sony Music Entertainment
summary: In a suit by music labels over an internet service provider's subscribers sharing copyrighted music, the Court held the provider was not contributorily liable for its users' infringement and reversed the Fourth Circuit.

title: Craig v. Boren
summary: The Court ruled that statutory or administrative sex classifications were subject to intermediate scrutiny under the Fourteenth Amendment's Equal Protection Clause.

title: Crosby v. National Foreign Trade Council
summary: The Court unanimously struck down, under the federal preemption doctrine, a Massachusetts law that barred state agencies from buying goods and services from companies doing business with Myanmar (Burma).

title: CSX Transportation, Inc. v. Alabama Department of Revenue
summary: The Court held that a railroad could challenge a state's sales and use taxes as discriminatory under the Railroad Revitalization and Regulatory Reform Act of 1976 when the tax was imposed on railroads but not their main competitors.

title: CSX Transportation, Inc. v. Georgia State Board of Equalization
summary: The Court held that the Railroad Revitalization and Regulatory Reform Act of 1976 allows a railroad to try to show that state methods of valuing railroad property result in a discriminatory determination of true market value.

title: Cullen v. Pinholster
summary: The Court held that in federal habeas proceedings under § 2254(d)(1), only evidence presented to the state court that adjudicated the claim on the merits could be considered, and that the respondent was not entitled to the habeas relief the Ninth Circuit had granted.

title: Cummings v. Premier Rehab Keller, P.L.L.C.
Cyan, Inc. v. Beaver County Employees Retirement Fund
Daimler AG v. Bauman
summary: The Court considered whether a U.S. court may exercise jurisdiction over a foreign company because its subsidiary acts for it in the forum state, and held that American courts lacked jurisdiction over claims based on conduct outside the United States.

title: Dart Cherokee Basin Operating Co. v. Owens
summary: In a dispute over removing a class action over oil and gas lease revenue from Kansas state court to federal court, the Court held that a notice of removal did not need to include evidence of the amount in controversy.

title: Dastar Corp. v. Twentieth Century Fox Film Corp.
Davis v. Mann
summary: The Court, in one of a series of 1964 cases, ruled that state legislature districts had to be roughly equal in population.

title: Davis v. United States (1990)
summary: The Court ruled that parents' payments toward their sons' missionary expenses for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints could not be treated as "charitable contributions" under the tax regulation.

title: Dawson Chemical Co. v. Rohm & Haas Co.
summary: The Court, in a case on patent misuse and the 1952 patent law amendments, held that supplying an unpatented product especially adapted for a patented process and lacking substantial non-infringing use was unlawful contributory infringement.

title: De Veau v. Braisted
summary: The Court ruled that an interstate compact restricting convicted felons from holding union office was not preempted by federal labor law, did not violate due process, and was not an ex post facto law or bill of attainder.

title: Dean Milk Co. v. City of Madison
Dean Witter Reynolds Inc. v. Byrd
summary: In a dispute between a brokerage firm and a former client, the Court held unanimously that the Federal Arbitration Act required state-law claims to be arbitrated when the parties had contracted to do so, even with parallel federal claims in court.

title: Decker v. Northwest Environmental Defense Center
summary: The Court held that a Clean Water Act provision governing challenges to EPA actions did not bar a citizen suit against an alleged violator seeking to enforce CWA obligations, and that the case was not moot despite interim regulations.

title: Department of Commerce v. New York
summary: In a dispute over adding a citizenship question to the 2020 census, the Court held that the Enumeration clause permits such a question but that the administration's explanation for adding it appeared contrived and pretextual.

title: Department of Homeland Security v. Thuraissigiam
summary: The Court ruled that the 1996 immigration law limiting habeas corpus judicial review of immigration officers' decisions did not violate the Suspension Clause of Article One of the U.S. Constitution.

title: Department of Justice v. Landano
summary: The Court held that the government was not entitled to a presumption that a source was confidential under Exemption 7(D) of the Freedom of Information Act whenever the source gave information to the FBI during a criminal investigation.

title: Department of Transportation v. Association of American Railroads
Department of Treasury, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco & Firearms v. Galioto
Descamps v. United States
summary: In a case about evaluating prior offenses under the Armed Career Criminal Act, the Court held that judges may only look at a crime's statutory elements, not the underlying facts, when the conviction crime has a single, indivisible set of elements.

title: Diamond v. Chakrabarty
summary: The Court considered whether living organisms can be patented and held that human-made bacteria could be patented under U.S. patent law because such an invention was a "manufacture" or "composition of matter".

title: Dillon v. United States
summary: The Court held that when a defendant received a resentencing hearing after the Sentencing Guidelines changed in the defendant's favor, the updated Guidelines were binding on the district court, though they could be merely advisory at a first sentencing.

title: District of Columbia Court of Appeals v. Feldman
District of Columbia v. Heller
summary: The Court ruled that the Second Amendment protects an individual's right to keep and bear arms for lawful purposes such as self-defense at home, and that the District of Columbia's handgun ban and trigger-lock requirement violated it.

title: District of Columbia v. John R. Thompson Co.
summary: The Court unanimously ruled that a cafeteria's segregating policies were illegal, in a case over the validity of 1872 and 1873 Acts that prohibited segregation in public places in the District of Columbia.

title: District of Columbia v. Tri County Industries, Inc.
Dollar General Corp. v. Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians
summary: In a dispute over whether a tribal court could hear a civil case against a non-Indian operating a Dollar General store on tribal land, the Court was equally divided and thereby affirmed the Fifth Circuit's holding that the tribal court had jurisdiction.

title: Domino's Pizza, Inc. v. McDonald
summary: In a case about racial discrimination claims under 42 U.S.C. § 1981, the Court ruled unanimously that agents of contracting parties lack personal rights under those contracts and so cannot state a section 1981 claim.

title: Douglas v. Independent Living Center of Southern California
summary: The Court, faced with plaintiffs claiming a Supremacy Clause right to sue to enforce federal Medicaid law against a conflicting state law, declined a firm decision and remanded to the Ninth Circuit because circumstances had changed during the appeal.

title: Dow Chemical Co. v. United States
Eastman Kodak Co. v. Image Technical Services, Inc.
summary: The Court held that an equipment manufacturer lacking significant market power in the primary equipment market could still have enough market power in the repair parts aftermarket to be liable under antitrust laws for exclusionary conduct there.

title: Edwards v. Aguillard
summary: The Court considered a Louisiana law requiring creation science to be taught whenever evolutionary science was taught in public schools, and ruled that it violated the Establishment Clause because it was intended to advance a particular religion.

title: Edwards v. South Carolina
summary: The Court ruled that the First and Fourteenth Amendments forbade state government officials from forcing a crowd to disperse when it was otherwise legally marching in front of a state house.

title: Elk Grove Unified School District v. Newdow
Empire HealthChoice Assurance, Inc. v. McVeigh
summary: The Court affirmed the Second Circuit's ruling against a health insurer that sought reimbursement of benefits paid to a deceased federal employee from his wife's settlement with third parties who allegedly caused his injuries.

title: Encino Motorcars v. Navarro
summary: The Court, in a dispute over whether automotive service advisors were eligible for overtime pay under the Fair Labor Standards Act, reversed the Ninth Circuit's ruling that the exemption did not include service advisors.

title: England v. Louisiana State Board of Medical Examiners
Entergy Corp. v. Riverkeeper Inc.
summary: In a dispute over EPA Clean Water Act rules on power plant cooling water intakes, the Court reversed the lower court and upheld as reasonable the EPA's decision to allow cost–benefit analysis in determining the best technology available.

title: Espinoza v. Farah Manufacturing Co.
summary: The Court held that an employer's refusal to hire a person because he is not a United States citizen is not employment discrimination based on "national origin" in violation of §703 of the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

title: Espinoza v. Montana Department of Revenue
Estelle v. Gamble
summary: The Court held that a prisoner claiming an Eighth Amendment violation under § 1983 must allege acts or omissions sufficiently harmful to show deliberate indifference to serious medical needs, and that medical malpractice alone is not cruel and unusual punishment.

title: Estelle v. Williams
summary: The Court reversed the Court of Appeals, which had found a due process violation when a defendant unable to post bail was tried in prison clothes, and reinstated his conviction for assaulting his former landlord.

title: Evans v. Chavis
summary: The Court held that, absent clear direction from the state supreme court on the timeliness of habeas filings, a federal appellate court must itself examine the delay in each case and determine what the state courts would have held about timeliness.

title: Evenwel v. Abbott
summary: The Court held that the one person, one vote principle under the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment allows states to use total population, not just total voting-eligible population, to draw legislative districts.

title: Exxon Mobil Corp. v. Corporación Cimex, S. A. (Cuba)
summary: The Court held that the Helms–Burton Act itself abrogated the sovereign immunity of Cuban agencies and instrumentalities, so plaintiffs suing them under the act did not also need to satisfy a Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act exception.

title: Exxon Mobil Corp. v. Saudi Basic Industries Corp.
F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd. v. Empagran S.A.
summary: The Court held that where price-fixing significantly harmed customers both abroad and in the United States, but the foreign harm was independent of any domestic harm, neither the FTAIA exception nor the Sherman Act applied to a claim based solely on the foreign harm.

title: Fay v. Noia
summary: The Court held that state prisoners were entitled to federal habeas relief even if they had not pursued a state-court remedy that was no longer available to them, unless they had deliberately bypassed the orderly procedure of state courts.

title: FCC v. AT&T Inc. (2026)
summary: The Court held that the FCC did not violate the Seventh Amendment by issuing forfeiture orders without a jury trial, because such orders do not definitively resolve legal obligations and the defendant keeps the right to a full de novo jury trial before paying.

title: FCC v. Prometheus Radio Project
summary: In a dispute over FCC media ownership rules under the Telecommunications Act of 1996, the Court unanimously ruled that the FCC had not acted arbitrarily and capriciously, reversing the Third Circuit and allowing it to relax cross-media ownership rules.

title: FDA v. Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine
summary: In a challenge to the FDA's approval of the abortion drug mifepristone, the Court unanimously held that the Alliance lacked Article III association standing because no legal injury was shown, and it reversed the lower court decisions.

title: Federal Bureau of Investigation v. Fazaga
summary: In a case over FBI surveillance and the state secrets privilege, the Court overturned the Ninth Circuit's ruling and held that FISA does not override the state secrets defense.

title: Federal Election Comm'n v. Colo. Republican Fed. Campaign Comm.
summary: In a challenge to a federal limit on party spending for congressional campaigns, the Court held that the party committee's expenditures, made independently of a specific candidate, did not violate FECA's contribution limits and were protected by the First Amendment.

title: Federal Power Commission v. Sierra Pacific Power Co.
Federal Republic of Germany v. Philipp
summary: The Court unanimously held that the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act did not allow Holocaust survivors' heirs to sue Germany in U.S. court over property taken during the Nazi era, because the sale was an expropriation of property.

title: Feres v. United States
summary: In a hearing combining three federal cases, the Court held that the United States was not liable under the Federal Tort Claims Act for injuries to armed forces members on active duty caused by the negligence of others in the armed forces.

title: Fernandez v. California
summary: The Court held that when an objecting co-resident is removed for objectively reasonable purposes, such as a lawful arrest, the remaining resident may validly consent to a search of the dwelling.

title: Fernandez-Vargas v. Gonzales
summary: The Court held that the reinstatement provision in §241(a)(5) applied to immigrants who illegally reentered the U.S. before IIRIRA's effective date, and that applying it to a man deported after reentering in 1982 was not impermissibly retroactive.

title: Festo Corp. v. Shoketsu Kinzoku Kogyo Kabushiki Co.
Fiallo v. Bell
summary: The Court rejected unmarried biological fathers' equal protection and due process challenges to immigration preference provisions that excluded their illegitimate children, and upheld the provisions, citing Congress' exceptionally broad power to admit or exclude noncitizens.

title: First Am. Fin. Corp. v. Edwards
First Options of Chicago, Inc. v. Kaplan
First Unitarian Church of Los Angeles
Fisher v. United States (1976)
summary: The Court held that the Fifth Amendment's self-incrimination clause did not protect a taxpayer or their attorney from being required to turn over workpapers prepared by the taxpayer's accountant.

title: Fisher v. University of Texas (2016)
summary: The Court held that the Fifth Circuit had correctly found that the University of Texas at Austin's race-conscious undergraduate admissions policy survived strict scrutiny.

title: Flora v. United States
summary: The Court held that a taxpayer generally must pay the full amount of an income tax deficiency assessed by the Commissioner before challenging its correctness in a federal district court refund suit.

title: Florida Lime & Avocado Growers, Inc. v. Paul
Florida Prepaid Postsecondary Education Expense Board v. College Savings Bank
Florida v. Georgia (2021)
summary: In a long-running dispute over water in the ACF River Basin, where Florida sought a cap on Georgia's water use, the Court overruled Florida's exceptions to the special master's report and unanimously dismissed the case.

title: Florida v. Harris
summary: The Court, addressing whether a drug-detection dog's training or certification suffices to establish probable cause for a vehicle search, unanimously held that certification by a bona fide organization after reliability testing in a controlled setting supports such reliability.

title: Florida v. Royer
summary: In a Fourth Amendment case about warrantless searches and seizures, the Court ruled that police may approach a person based on their behavior but, absent more, cannot detain or search that person without a warrant.

title: Florida v. Thomas
summary: In a case about the extent of New York v. Belton and automobile searches, the Court unanimously dismissed the case because the Florida state courts' decision was not final.

title: Flowers v. Mississippi
summary: In a case over peremptory challenges used to remove black jurors in a black man's murder trials, the Court ruled that the case fell under Batson and that the state inappropriately removed most of the potential black jurors.

title: Fogerty v. Fantasy, Inc.
summary: In a dispute over attorneys' fees under the Copyright Act of 1976, the Court held that such awards are discretionary and that the same standards apply to a prevailing plaintiff and a prevailing defendant.

title: Ford Motor Co. v. Montana Eighth Judicial District
summary: In product liability suits against an out-of-state manufacturer over accidents in Montana and Minnesota, the Court ruled that the claims arose out of or related to Ford's business and marketing activities, supporting the states' specific personal jurisdiction.

title: Ford Motor Co. v. United States
Ford v. Wainwright
summary: The Court upheld the common law rule that the insane cannot be executed, ruling that a petitioner is entitled to a competency evaluation and an evidentiary hearing in court on their competency to be executed.

title: Forest Grove School District v. T. A.
summary: The Court held that the IDEA authorizes reimbursement for private special education services when a public school fails to provide a free appropriate public education and the private placement is appropriate, even if the child had not previously received public special education services.

title: Fowler v. Rhode Island
summary: The Court held that a municipal ordinance used to penalize a Jehovah's Witnesses minister for preaching at a peaceful religious meeting in a public park, while other religious groups could hold services there, violated the First and Fourteenth Amendments.

title: Frank v. Gaos
summary: In a class action case about cy pres settlements, the Court remanded to the Ninth Circuit to address the plaintiffs' standing in light of Spokeo, Inc. v. Robins.

title: Frank v. Maryland
summary: The Court ruled in favor of health inspectors who sought to enter a man's home to check for a rat infestation, reasoning that the search would benefit the public more than it intruded on his privacy interests.

title: Franklin v. Massachusetts
summary: In a case about the 1990 Census, the Court held that the President is not an "agency" under the Administrative Procedure Act, so the Act does not authorize judicial review of actions Congress delegated to the President.

title: Free Enterprise Fund v. Public Company Accounting Oversight Board
summary: The Court ruled that laws insulating inferior officers from Presidential removal with two levels of "for cause" removal, as for Public Company Accounting Oversight Board officers under Sarbanes–Oxley, violated Article Two of the Constitution.

title: Freedman v. Maryland
summary: In a case over government-operated film rating boards, the Court ruled that a board could only approve a film, not ban it, and had to approve a film within a reasonable time or go to court to stop its showing in theatres.

title: Fry v. Napoleon Community Schools
summary: The Court held that the Handicapped Children's Protection Act of 1986 did not require exhaustion of IDEA's state-level administrative remedies when the gravamen of the lawsuit was not the denial of a free appropriate public education.

title: Fry v. Pliler
summary: In AEDPA proceedings, the Court held that a federal court must assess the prejudicial impact of constitutional error in a state criminal trial under the "substantial and injurious effect" standard, whether or not the state appellate court reviewed it for harmlessness.

title: FTC v. Motion Picture Advertising Service Co.
summary: The Court held that exclusive output contracts used by four major companies, which foreclosed 75 percent of available outlets to competitors, fell within the Sherman Act's prohibitions and were an unfair method of competition under § 5 of the FTC Act.

title: FTC v. Ruberoid Co.
summary: The Court held that the Federal Trade Commission has broad discretion to fashion cease and desist orders for Robinson–Patman Act violations, and that reviewing courts should not modify its remedy unless it bears no reasonable relation to the unlawful practices found.

title: Garner v. Louisiana
summary: The Court unanimously ruled that Louisiana could not convict peaceful sit-in protesters who refused to leave dining establishments under the state's "disturbing the peace" laws.

title: Garza v. Idaho
summary: The Court held that the presumption of prejudice for Sixth Amendment purposes applies regardless of whether a defendant has waived the right to appeal.

title: Gebser v. Lago Vista Independent School District
summary: In a case about a teacher's sexual harassment of a student, the Court held that a school district may be liable, but damages under Title IX require that an official with authority had actual knowledge and was deliberately indifferent.

title: General Dynamics Corp. v. United States
Georgia v. Ashcroft
summary: The Court found that a three-judge district court panel failed to consider all the relevant factors when assessing whether Georgia's 2001 State Senate redistricting plan caused retrogression of black voters' effective exercise of the franchise under Section 5 of the Voting Rights Act.

title: Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org, Inc.
summary: The Court ruled that the Official Code of Georgia Annotated could not be copyrighted, because its annotations were authored by an arm of the legislature in the course of its legislative duties and so fell under the government edicts doctrine.

title: Gideon v. Wainwright
summary: The Court ruled that the Sixth Amendment requires states to provide attorneys to criminal defendants who cannot afford their own, extending the right to counsel from the federal government to the states.

title: Gill v. Whitford
summary: In a challenge to Wisconsin's redistricting plan as a partisan gerrymander, the Court remanded the case to the lower courts, finding that the plaintiffs had not demonstrated standing because they had not shown harm.

title: Glacier Northwest, Inc. v. Teamsters
summary: In a dispute over an employer's power to sue a labor union for destruction of property following a strike, the Court concluded that the National Labor Relations Act did not preempt the lawsuits against the union, allowing litigation to continue.

title: Global-Tech Appliances, Inc. v. SEB S.A.
summary: The Court held that inducing patent infringement requires knowledge of the infringement, but affirmed the Federal Circuit's judgment against the petitioners under the doctrine of willful blindness, given their knowledge of a related infringement lawsuit.

title: Gonzaga University v. Doe
summary: The Court ruled that the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act of 1974, which bars federal funding of schools that release education records to unauthorized persons, creates no right enforceable under 42 U.S.C. § 1983.

title: Gonzales v. Carhart
summary: In a challenge to the Partial-Birth Abortion Ban Act of 2003, the Court upheld the federal ban, holding that it did not impose an undue burden on women's due process right to obtain an abortion.

title: Gonzales v. Raich
summary: The Court ruled that, under the Commerce Clause, Congress may criminalize the production and use of homegrown cannabis even where state law allows its use for medicinal purposes.

title: Good News Club v. Milford Central School
summary: The Court held that a public school's exclusion of a club from its limited public forum based solely on the club's religious nature was impermissible viewpoint discrimination.

title: Google LLC v. Oracle America, Inc.
summary: In a dispute over Google's use of Java APIs in Android, the Court ruled that Google's use fell within fair use, bypassed the copyrightability question, reversed the Federal Circuit, and remanded the case.

title: Graham v. John Deere Co.
summary: The Court clarified the nonobviousness requirement in patent law, confirming that non-obviousness is a question of law but holding that §103 required determining factual questions to resolve obviousness.

title: Granholm v. Heald
summary: The Court ruled that New York and Michigan laws letting in-state wineries ship wine directly to consumers while barring out-of-state wineries from doing so were unconstitutional.

title: Gratz v. Bollinger
summary: In a challenge to the University of Michigan's undergraduate affirmative action admissions policy, the Court ruled that the point system awarding 20 points to underrepresented minorities was unconstitutional because it prevented individualized assessment of diversity contributions.

title: Gravel v. United States
summary: In a case about the protections of the Speech or Debate Clause, the Court held that the clause's privileges and immunities for members of Congress also extend to Congressional aides, but not to activity outside the legislative process.

title: Graver Tank & Manufacturing Co. v. Linde Air Products Co.
Great Lakes Insurance SE v. Raiders Retreat Realty Co.
Green Tree Financial Corp.-Alabama v. Randolph
Greene v. Fisher
summary: In a habeas case under AEDPA, the Court unanimously ruled that "clearly established Federal law" does not include Supreme Court decisions announced after the last state-court adjudication on the merits but before the conviction became final.

title: Greer v. Spock
summary: The Court upheld military regulations strictly forbidding partisan political activity on unrestricted areas of a military base, Fort Dix, against a First Amendment challenge.

title: Gregory v. Ashcroft
summary: The Court considered whether a Missouri constitutional provision requiring state judges to retire at age 70 conflicted with the federal ADEA and the Equal Protection Clause, and it upheld the provision.

title: Griggs v. Duke Power Co.
summary: In an employment discrimination case, the Court ruled that the company's employment requirements did not pertain to applicants' ability to perform the job and so unintentionally discriminated against black employees.

title: Groff v. DeJoy
summary: In a Title VII religious accommodation dispute, the Court unanimously ruled for the employee, generally upholding Trans World but clarifying that more than de minimis costs do not show undue hardship; employers must show substantial increased costs.

title: Gross v. FBL Financial Services, Inc.
Guam v. United States
summary: In a dispute over who paid to clean up the Ordot Dump on Guam, the Court ruled unanimously that Guam had timely filed its Superfund suit to recover part of the cleanup costs from the United States, so the case could proceed.

title: Gunn v. University Committee to End the War in Viet Nam
Haaland v. Brackeen
summary: In a challenge by Texas, Louisiana, Indiana and individual plaintiffs to the Indian Child Welfare Act, the Court held the Act consistent with congressional powers, rejected the state commandeering claims, and made no ruling on the Fourteenth Amendment claims for lack of standing.

title: Halbert v. Michigan
summary: The Court held that a Michigan law denying public counsel to defendants appealing a conviction based on a plea violated the equal protection and due process clauses of the Fourteenth Amendment.

title: Halliburton Co. v. Erica P. John Fund, Inc.
Hamdan v. Rumsfeld
summary: The Court held that military commissions set up by the Bush administration to try Guantanamo Bay detainees violated both the Uniform Code of Military Justice and the Geneva Conventions ratified by the U.S.

title: Hamilton v. Alabama (1961)
summary: In a case where a man was convicted and sentenced to death in Alabama, the Court ruled unanimously that the absence of counsel at his arraignment violated his Fourteenth Amendment due process rights.

title: Hanna v. Plumer
summary: In a diversity case about whether federal rules on service of process or state rules should govern, the Court ruled that federal courts shall apply the federal rule under the facts of the case.

title: Harper & Row v. Nation Enterprises
summary: The Court held that The Nation's quoting and summarizing of President Ford's forthcoming memoir was not fair use, rejecting its public-interest argument because the right of first publication was important enough to favor Harper & Row.

title: Harrington v. Purdue Pharma L.P.
summary: The Court ruled in a Chapter 11 dispute over a release extinguishing nondebtors' claims against nondebtor third parties without consent, holding that the Bankruptcy Code did not authorize it and blocking the bankruptcy plan.

title: Harris v. Viegelahn
summary: The Court unanimously held that a debtor who earns money after filing Chapter 13 bankruptcy and converts to Chapter 7 before the money is sent to creditors is permitted to keep those funds.

title: Harte-Hanks Communications, Inc. v. Connaughton
summary: In a libel case brought by a public figure, the Court held that departure from responsible reporting alone was not enough for damages, but that reckless disregard for the truth, including ignoring obvious sources, could support damages for actual malice.

title: Hartman v. Moore
summary: The Court ruled that a plaintiff claiming a prosecution was brought in retaliation for First Amendment speech against postal policy must allege and prove that the criminal charges were brought without probable cause.

title: Havens Realty Corp. v. Coleman
summary: The Court held that an organization may sue in its own right if directly injured, such as through a "drain on the organization's resources," and that "testers" who sought to determine whether a company violated the law may have standing in their own right.

title: Hazelwood School District v. United States
Health & Hospital Corp. of Marion County v. Talevski
Heath v. Alabama
summary: The Court ruled that, under the dual sovereignty doctrine, the Fifth Amendment's double jeopardy clause did not bar one state from prosecuting and punishing someone already convicted and sentenced for the same act in another state.

title: Heck v. Humphrey
summary: The Court held that a §1983 plaintiff seeking damages for an allegedly unconstitutional conviction or imprisonment must prove the conviction or sentence was reversed, expunged, declared invalid by a state tribunal, or called into question by a federal writ of habeas corpus.

title: Heffernan v. City of Paterson
summary: In a case about a police detective disciplined for apparently supporting a mayoral challenger, the Court held that a public employee's constitutional rights might be violated when an employer disciplines them over a mistaken belief that they engaged in protected speech.

title: Heimeshoff v. Hartford Life & Accident Insurance Co.
summary: The Court considered when the agreed-upon limitations period for challenging a long-term disability denial began, and unanimously ruled that the period was not too short, no statute prevented it, and courts must enforce it and its start date as written in the plan.

title: Henry Schein, Inc. v. Archer & White Sales, Inc.
summary: The Court unanimously held that the "wholly groundless" exception to arbitrability violated the Federal Arbitration Act, so a valid delegation of arbitrability to an arbitrator must be honored even if a court thinks the argument for arbitration is wholly groundless.

title: Hernandez v. Mesa
summary: The Court held, in a case over a U.S. Border Patrol agent's shooting of a Mexican teenager across the border, that the Bivens precedent did not extend to claims based on cross-border shootings.

title: Hess v. Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corp.
summary: The Court considered whether the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey was an "arm of the state" entitled to Eleventh Amendment sovereign immunity and held that it was not.

title: Hiibel v. Sixth Judicial District Court of Nevada
summary: The Court held that a statute requiring suspects to disclose their names during a valid Terry stop did not violate the Fourth Amendment if it first required reasonable suspicion, nor the Fifth Amendment absent any allegation that the name could incriminate.

title: Hills v. Gautreaux
summary: The case involved Chicago families in housing projects who received Section 8 vouchers to move to the suburbs, and the Court ruled that the housing department had violated the Fifth Amendment and the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

title: Hodges v. United States
summary: The Court overturned the convictions of three white men who conspired against black sawmill workers, holding that Congress lacked the power under the Thirteenth Amendment to intervene against racially motivated interference with labor contracts.

title: Holder v. Gutierrez
summary: The Court held that the Board of Immigration Appeals permissibly construed the statute in requiring a non-citizen seeking cancellation of a deportation order to individually satisfy lawful permanent resident requirements, rather than relying on a parent's years of status.

title: Holder v. Humanitarian Law Project
summary: The Court ruled against a group that wanted to help designated foreign terrorist organizations learn to resolve conflicts peacefully, holding that the Patriot Act's ban on providing material support, including training and expert advice, covered such assistance.

title: Hollingsworth v. Perry
summary: In a challenge to California's ballot initiative banning same-sex marriage, the Court held that the initiative's official sponsors lacked Article III standing to appeal an adverse federal court ruling.

title: Hope v. Pelzer
summary: The Court ruled that qualified immunity did not apply to a lawsuit challenging the Alabama Department of Corrections's use of the "hitching post," a punishment in which inmates were immobilized for long periods.

title: Horne v. Department of Agriculture
summary: In a dispute over a rule requiring farmers to keep part of their raisin crops off the market, the Court held that the farmer had standing to sue under the Takings Clause and that the National Raisin Reserve violated the Takings Clause.

title: Houston Community College System v. Wilson
summary: The Court unanimously held that a local government board member's First Amendment freedom of speech was not abridged when his colleagues verbally censured him.

title: Hudson v. Michigan
summary: The Court held that a violation of the Fourth Amendment's knock-and-announce requirement for police entering a private residence does not require suppression of the evidence obtained in the ensuing search.

title: Hughes v. Alexandria Scrap Corp.
summary: The Court determined that Maryland, which acted as a market participant rather than a regulator in its program to reduce abandoned cars, could favor its own citizens over out-of-state ones without violating the Dormant Commerce Clause.

title: Husted v. Randolph Institute
summary: The Court ruled that Ohio's voter list-maintenance process, which used voter inactivity to trigger a confirmation notice before removal from the rolls, did not violate federal voter registration laws.

title: Iancu v. Brunetti
summary: The Court held that the Lanham Act provisions barring registration of "immoral" or "scandalous" trademarks were unconstitutional because they let the Patent & Trademark Office engage in viewpoint discrimination, violating the First Amendment's Free Speech Clause.

title: Idaho v. United States
summary: In a dispute over ownership of lands submerged under Lake Coeur d'Alene and the St. Joe River, the Court held that the United States, not Idaho, held title, in trust for the Coeur d'Alene Tribe as part of its reservation.

title: Illinois v. Allen
summary: The Court ruled, in a case about removing an unruly criminal defendant during trial, that a judge may remove a stubbornly defiant defendant from the courtroom after warning that continued disruption will lead to removal.

title: Illinois v. Gates
summary: In a Fourth Amendment case about probable cause, the Court overruled two earlier decisions and replaced the Aguilar–Spinelli test with a "totality of the circumstances" test.

title: Illinois v. McArthur
summary: In a case about the government's power to limit a person's control of their home pending a search warrant, the Court held the search was not unconstitutional because police reasonably needed to prevent destruction of evidence.

title: Immigration and Naturalization Service v. Aguirre-Aguirre
summary: In an immigration dispute, the Court determined that federal courts had to defer to the Board of Immigration Appeals's interpretation of the Immigration and Nationality Act.

title: Immigration and Naturalization Service v. St. Cyr
Immigration and Naturalization Service v. Stevic
Impression Products, Inc. v. Lexmark International, Inc.
summary: In a patent suit over refilled and resold ink cartridges, the Court held that under the exhaustion doctrine a patent holder cannot sue for infringement over further use of an item after selling it, reversing the Federal Circuit.

title: Intel Corp. Investment Policy Committee v. Sulyma
summary: The Court held that, under ERISA's requirement that plaintiffs with "actual knowledge" of a fiduciary breach sue within three years, a plaintiff does not necessarily have actual knowledge of disclosures he received but did not read or cannot recall reading.

title: Intel Corp. v. Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.
Inyo County v. Paiute-Shoshone Indians of the Bishop Community
Island Trees School District v. Pico
Jacobson v. United States
summary: The Court overturned a Nebraska man's conviction for receiving child sexual abuse material through the mail, ruling that postal inspectors had implanted the desire to do so through repeated written entreaties, which amounted to entrapment.

title: Jam v. International Finance Corp.
summary: The Court ruled that international organizations, such as the International Finance Corporation, could be sued in US federal courts for conduct arising from their commercial activities, sharing the same immunity as foreign governments.

title: James v. United States (2007)
summary: The Court held that attempted burglary could serve as a predicate felony under the federal Armed Career Criminal Act, which required a mandatory minimum 15-year term for felons in possession of firearms with three prior qualifying convictions.

title: Janus v. AFSCME
summary: The Court ruled that fees collected by labor unions from non-members in the public sector violate the First Amendment right to free speech, overruling its 1977 decision in Abood v. Detroit Board of Education.

title: Jefferson Parish Hospital District No. 2 v. Hyde
Jencks v. United States
summary: The Court held that the federal government must produce documents relied upon by government witnesses in federal criminal proceedings, in a case where a union president was convicted of filing a false non-Communist affidavit.

title: Jenkins v. Georgia
summary: The Court ruled that Georgia had gone too far in classifying the film Carnal Knowledge as obscene under the Miller standard, and it overturned the theatre manager's conviction for distributing obscene material.

title: Jennings v. Stephens
summary: In a federal habeas proceeding, the Court held that a criminal defendant may defend the district court's judgment on alternative grounds without a cross-appeal or certificate of appealability, unless doing so would enlarge the defendant's rights under the judgment.

title: Jesner v. Arab Bank, PLC
summary: In a suit alleging a bank facilitated terrorist attacks by transferring funds, the Court held that foreign corporations cannot be sued under the Alien Tort Statute.

title: Johnson v. Arteaga-Martinez
summary: The Court held that Section 1231(a)(6) of the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 does not require bond hearings, with the government bearing the burden by clear and convincing evidence, for noncitizens detained for six months.

title: Johnson v. Williams
summary: The Court held that under the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act, when a state court rejects some of a defendant's claims but does not expressly address a federal claim, a federal habeas court must presume, subject to rebuttal, that the claim was adjudicated on the merits.

title: Jones v. Alfred H. Mayer Co.
summary: The Court held that the Civil Rights Act of 1866, as codified in 42 U.S.C. § 1982, barred both private and public racial discrimination in the sale or rental of property, a valid exercise of Congress's Thirteenth Amendment power.

title: Jones v. Harris Associates
summary: In a dispute where investors claimed their investment advisor's fees were too steep, the Court held that courts may regulate mutual fund advisers' fees under the Investment Company Act of 1940 when the fees are excessive and breach fiduciary duty.

title: Jones v. Mississippi
summary: The Court upheld a juvenile offender's life sentence without parole, ruling that states have discretion to impose such sentences on juveniles without making a separate assessment of their permanent incorrigibility.

title: Joseph Burstyn, Inc. v. Wilson
summary: The Court held that New York Education Law provisions letting a censor forbid commercial showing of films deemed "sacrilegious" were a restraint on freedom of speech and violated the First Amendment, overturning its earlier Mutual Film decision.

title: Judulang v. Holder
