summary: The Court unanimously invalidated the Board of Immigration Appeals' "comparable-grounds rule," used to decide whether certain long-term resident aliens facing deportation over a prior conviction could seek relief, as arbitrary and capricious.

title: Kansas v. Carr
summary: In a case on sentencing procedures in capital cases, the Court held that judges need not affirmatively instruct juries on the burden of proof for mitigating evidence, and that joint trials of capital defendants are often preferable.

title: Katzenbach v. McClung
summary: The Court unanimously held that Congress acted within its Commerce Clause power when it forbade racial discrimination in restaurants, because such discrimination burdened interstate commerce.

title: Kaufman v. United States
summary: The Court held that criminal defendants could raise claims that evidence was obtained in violation of the Fourth Amendment in a collateral attack under the federal habeas corpus statute, overruling the Eighth Circuit's contrary decision.

title: Kelly v. United States
summary: In a case over politically motivated George Washington Bridge lane closures, the Court unanimously overturned the fraud and conspiracy convictions because the scheme did not aim to obtain money or property, and remanded to the lower courts.

title: Kent v. Dulles
summary: The Court held that the government violated the right to travel and First Amendment free speech rights when it suspended people's passports based on their political speech.

title: Keyes v. School District No. 1, Denver
summary: The Court, in a suit by black and Hispanic parents over segregation in Denver schools, found that the school board intentionally created and maintained segregated core city schools, so the entire district had to be desegregated.

title: Keystone Bituminous Coal Ass'n v. DeBenedictis
summary: In a Fifth Amendment Takings Clause case, the Court upheld a Pennsylvania statute that limited coal mining causing subsidence damage to buildings, dwellings, and cemeteries.

title: Kimmelman v. Morrison
summary: The Court rejected the prosecution's argument that a habeas petition raising ineffective assistance of counsel was a back-door Fourth Amendment claim, holding the two issues were distinct and the petition could go forward.

title: King v. Burwell
summary: In a dispute over Affordable Care Act provisions, the Court upheld the payment of premium tax credits to qualifying persons in all states, including those with exchanges established by the Department of Health and Human Services rather than by a state.

title: Kirtsaeng v. John Wiley & Sons, Inc. (2016)
summary: The Court held that when deciding whether to award attorney's fees under the Copyright Act's fee-shifting provision, a district court should give substantial weight to the objective reasonableness of the losing party's position while considering all other relevant circumstances.

title: Kloeckner v. Solis
summary: In a dispute over where "mixed case" appeals involving wrongful termination and discrimination claims go from the Merit Systems Protection Board, the Court unanimously held that the statute clearly provided for appeal to a federal district court.

title: Knetsch v. United States
summary: The Court ruled for the IRS and denied a taxpayer's claimed deduction on money he borrowed to buy a tax-deferred annuity.

title: Knox v. Service Employees International Union, Local 1000
Koontz v. St. Johns River Water Management District
summary: In a dispute over conditions on development permits, the Court held that land-use agencies must meet the nexus and rough proportionality standards even when the condition is a payment of money or the permit is denied for refusing the condition.

title: Kramer v. Union Free School District No. 15
KSR International Co. v. Teleflex Inc.
Kurns v. Railroad Friction Products Corp.
Lackawanna County District Attorney v. Coss
summary: The Court held that a prisoner could not challenge his current sentence on the ground that it was enhanced by an unconstitutional prior conviction, basing its decision on a reading of the statute rather than the Sixth Amendment.

title: Lackey v. Stinnie
summary: The Court held that winning a preliminary injunction under the Civil Rights Attorney's Fees Award Act of 1976 did not make litigants a "prevailing party" entitled to attorney's fees, even when the case became moot after the challenged law was repealed.

title: Lakeside v. Oregon
summary: The Court ruled that trial judges may instruct a jury not to draw any inference of guilt from a defendant's refusal to testify, even when the defendant objects to the instruction.

title: Landor v. Louisiana Department of Corrections and Public Safety
LaRue v. DeWolff, Boberg & Associates, Inc.
summary: The Court held that ERISA gives no remedy for individual injuries distinct from plan injuries, but does let a person with a retirement account recover from a manager whose fiduciary breaches impaired the value of plan assets in that person's individual account.

title: Leary v. United States
summary: The Court unanimously declared the Marihuana Tax Act unconstitutional in a challenge by a man arrested for marijuana possession who argued the act required self-incrimination, and it overturned his conviction.

title: Ledbetter v. Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co.
LeDure v. Union Pacific Railroad Company
Lefkowitz v. Newsome
summary: The Court held that when state law lets a defendant plead guilty while keeping the right to judicial review of specified constitutional issues, the defendant may still pursue those claims in a federal habeas corpus proceeding.

title: Legal Services Corp. v. Velazquez
summary: The Court ruled that congressional restrictions barring Legal Services Corporation attorneys from representing clients seeking to challenge existing welfare law violated the First Amendment's free speech guarantees.

title: Lemon v. Kurtzman
summary: The Court ruled that Pennsylvania's 1968 act and Rhode Island's 1969 act, which reimbursed private, mostly Catholic, schools for teachers' salaries, were unconstitutional because they violated the Establishment Clause of the First Amendment.

title: Levy v. Louisiana
summary: The Court held that an illegitimate child's right to recover for a deceased parent could not be denied merely because of illegitimacy, since such a law would violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

title: Lewis v. Lewis & Clark Marine, Inc.
Lexmark International, Inc. v. Static Control Components, Inc.
summary: The Court unanimously affirmed the Sixth Circuit's ruling that a toner cartridge component maker had standing under the Lanham Act to sue printer company Lexmark for false advertising.

title: Life Technologies Corp. v. Promega Corp.
summary: The Court, in a case about selling components of patented inventions in foreign markets, held that supplying a single component abroad is not a substantial portion of the components that can give rise to liability under the Patent Act of 1952.

title: Limtiaco v. Camacho
summary: In a dispute over whether the Guam Organic Act's debt ceiling should be calculated using real market value or tax assessed value of property, the Court reversed the Guam Supreme Court and found for the Attorney General's office.

title: Linda R. S. v. Richard D.
summary: The Court ruled that a particular section of a Texas Penal Code did not apply to mothers with out-of-wedlock children, in a dispute between the mother and the father of such a child.

title: Lindke v. Freed
summary: In a dispute over individuals blocked from a public official's personal social media account, the Court unanimously held that the official's private posts were not state action, so blocking was allowed unless the official had authority to speak for the government and purported to do so.

title: Little Sisters of the Poor Saints Peter and Paul Home v. Pennsylvania
summary: In a dispute over new rules exempting groups with religious or moral objections from the ACA's contraceptive mandate, the Court ruled the rules were valid, as the departments had authority to issue them and the process did not violate the APA.

title: Liu v. Securities and Exchange Commission
summary: The Court ruled that courts may award the SEC's sought disgorgement for fraudulent activities as equitable relief, but only up to the wrongdoer's net profits and only for victims.

title: Locke v. Karass
summary: The Court held that the Constitution permits a local labor union chapter to charge non-members a service fee covering non-local litigation expenses if they are appropriately related to collective bargaining and the local and national unions have a reciprocal relationship.

title: Lockhart v. United States (2016)
summary: The Court interpreted a federal statute imposing a 10-year minimum sentence for child pornography possession after certain prior state convictions, holding that "involving a minor or ward" modifies only the last item in the series, and upheld the sentence.

title: Lockyer v. Andrade
summary: The Court held that habeas corpus relief was unavailable for a claim that a sentence under California's three strikes law was an unconstitutionally disproportionate punishment barred by the Eighth Amendment's ban on cruel and unusual punishments.

title: Lomax v. Ortiz-Marquez
summary: The Court unanimously held that, for a prisoner seeking to proceed in forma pauperis under the "3 strikes" system of 28 U.S.C. § 1915(g), a dismissal without prejudice for failure to state a claim counts as a strike.

title: Long Island Care at Home, Ltd. v. Coke
Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo
summary: In an administrative law dispute brought by fishing companies challenging a fisheries service rule, the Court overruled Chevron deference and assigned the determination of statutory ambiguity to the courts instead of deferring to agencies.

title: Lopez v. Davis
summary: The Court upheld a Bureau of Prisons regulation that reduced prisoners' sentences for completing a substance abuse program, even though the statute restricted the credit to those who did not commit a firearm-aided felony.

title: Lorain Journal Co. v. United States
summary: The Court held that a newspaper publisher who refused advertising from those who also advertised on a competing local radio station had attempted to monopolize trade in violation of § 2 of the Sherman Act and was properly enjoined.

title: Loretto v. Teleprompter Manhattan CATV Corp.
summary: The Court held that a governmental action amounting to a permanent physical occupation of property effects a regulatory taking to the extent of the occupation, regardless of any important public benefit or minimal economic impact on the owner.

title: Lorillard Tobacco Co. v. Reilly
summary: The Court held that a Massachusetts ban on tobacco advertising and sales near schools and playgrounds, challenged by a tobacco company on First Amendment grounds, was overbroad and also preempted by federal law.

title: Los Angeles County Flood Control District v. Natural Resources Defense Council, Inc.
summary: The Court unanimously reversed and remanded the Ninth Circuit, holding that water flowing from an improved portion of a navigable waterway into an unimproved portion of it is not a "discharge of a pollutant" under the Clean Water Act.

title: Lotus Development Corp. v. Borland International, Inc.
summary: In a dispute over whether software copyright covers a program's user interface such as menus, the Court, split evenly with one justice recused, left the lower court's decision affirmed without setting national precedent.

title: Louisiana ex rel. Francis v. Resweber
summary: The Court held that attempting a second execution of a man in the electric chair, after the first attempt failed, did not constitute double jeopardy or cruel and unusual punishment.

title: Louisiana v. Callais
summary: The Court, in a challenge to Louisiana's new congressional map that created two majority-minority districts, affirmed the district panel's judgment that the map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander under the Fifteenth Amendment.

title: Lujan v. Defenders of Wildlife
summary: The Court held that a group of American wildlife conservation and other environmental organizations lacked standing to challenge regulations jointly issued by the Secretaries of the Interior and Commerce.

title: Luna Perez v. Sturgis Public Schools
summary: The Court held that an ADA lawsuit seeking compensatory damages for denial of a free and appropriate public education could proceed without exhausting IDEA's administrative procedures, because IDEA does not offer compensatory damages.

title: M.L.B. v. S.L.J.
summary: The Court ruled for a mother whose parental rights were terminated and who could not afford record preparation fees, holding that a court may not bar an appeal in parental rights cases because of a party's financial means.

title: Madsen v. Women's Health Center, Inc.
summary: The Court considered a First Amendment challenge by antiabortion protesters to a Florida state court injunction limiting their demonstrations outside an abortion clinic, and it affirmed in part and reversed in part.

title: Mahanoy Area School District v. B.L.
summary: The Court ruled for a student who was suspended from cheerleading over an off-campus profane Snapchat post, holding that the school's interest in preventing disruption under Tinker did not overcome her First Amendment rights.

title: Maine Community Health Options v. United States
summary: In a dispute over unpaid Affordable Care Act Risk Corridors payments to unprofitable insurers, the Court ruled that Congress's appropriations riders did not cancel the government's obligation to pay, and that the insurers properly sought relief under the Tucker Act.

title: Mapp v. Ohio
summary: The Court ruled that the exclusionary rule, which bars prosecutors from using evidence obtained in violation of the Fourth Amendment, also applies to the states.

title: Marchioro v. Chaney
summary: The Court held that a state statute requiring each major political party to have a State Committee of two persons from each county did not violate party members' First and Fourteenth Amendment freedom of association regarding purely internal party decisions.

title: Marquez v. Screen Actors Guild Inc.
Marrama v. Citizens Bank of Massachusetts
Martin v. Ohio
summary: The Court held that in a criminal case the requirement that the prosecution prove each element of a crime beyond a reasonable doubt applies only to elements of the offense, not to justification, so states could place the burden of proving justification on the defense.

title: Martin v. United States
summary: In a suit under the Federal Tort Claims Act over an FBI raid on the wrong house, the Court unanimously vacated the Eleventh Circuit's dismissal and remanded the case for further proceedings.

title: Maryland v. Buie
summary: The Court held that the Fourth Amendment permitted a properly limited protective sweep during an in-home arrest when the officer reasonably believed, based on specific and articulable facts, that the area harbored a person posing a danger to those at the scene.

title: Maryland v. Louisiana
summary: The Court ruled in favor of Maryland, which had challenged a Louisiana tax law on natural gas extracted within the state as violating the Commerce Clause.

title: Massachusetts v. Environmental Protection Agency
summary: In a suit by Massachusetts, other states and cities to force the EPA to regulate greenhouse gas emissions under the Clean Air Act, the Court ruled for the plaintiffs, finding that greenhouse gases qualify as air pollutants.

title: Masterpiece Cakeshop v. Colorado Civil Rights Commission
summary: The Court, in a case over a bakery's refusal to make a custom wedding cake for a gay couple, ruled that the Commission showed hostility toward the owner's religious objections, violated his free exercise rights, and reversed its decision.

title: Matal v. Tam
summary: The Court unanimously affirmed the Federal Circuit's judgment that the Lanham Act provisions barring registration of trademarks that may "disparage" persons, institutions, beliefs, or national symbols violated the First Amendment.

title: Matrixx Initiatives, Inc. v. Siracusano
summary: In a securities fraud class action over a drugmaker's failure to disclose adverse event reports lacking statistically significant evidence of causation, the Court affirmed the Ninth Circuit and held the plaintiffs had stated a claim under §10(b) and Rule 10b-5.

title: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co. v. Zenith Radio Corp.
summary: In an antitrust case over whether Matsushita and other Japanese television manufacturers had a horizontal agreement, the Court held that evidence must tend to exclude the possibility of independent action to survive summary judgment.

title: McCollum v. Board of Education
summary: In a challenge to a "released time" program letting public school class time be used for religious instruction, the Court struck down the Champaign, Illinois, program as unconstitutional because of the school system's involvement in administering and supporting the classes.

title: McCreary County v. American Civil Liberties Union
summary: The Court ruled that Ten Commandments displays at two Kentucky county courthouses, challenged under the Establishment Clause, were unconstitutional.

title: McCutcheon v. Federal Election Commission
summary: The Court held unconstitutional a provision of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 that limited the total contributions an individual could make over a two-year period to all national party and federal candidate committees.

title: McDonough Power Equipment, Inc. v. Greenwood
McGirt v. Oklahoma
summary: The Court held that the land Congress reserved for the Muscogee Nation in the 19th century was never disestablished and is Indian country under the Major Crimes Act, so Oklahoma could not prosecute American Indians for crimes committed there.

title: MCI Telecommunications Corp. v. AT&T Co.
summary: The Court held that the FCC's statutory authority to "modify" requirements did not allow it to set aside the requirement that common carriers file tariffs with fixed terms and prices.

title: McWilliams v. Dunn
summary: The Court held that when the conditions of Ake v. Oklahoma are met, the state must give a defendant access to a mental health expert who is sufficiently available and independent from the prosecution to examine and assist the defense.

title: Meachum v. Fano
summary: In a case about prisoners' due process rights, the Court held that the Fourteenth Amendment's Due Process Clause did not give a prisoner a right to a fact-finding hearing before transfer to a facility with significantly more unfavorable conditions.

title: MeadWestvaco Corp. v. Illinois Department of Revenue
Menominee Tribe of Wisconsin v. United States
summary: In a case about when litigants may receive equitable tolling of a statute of limitations, the Court unanimously held the plaintiff was not entitled to tolling because it did not show "extraordinary circumstances" prevented timely filing.

title: Merck KGaA v. Integra Lifesciences I, Ltd.
summary: The Court held, in a dispute over the FDA safe harbor patent exemption, that basic research without intent to develop a particular drug is not covered, but the exemption does not categorically exclude experimentation on drugs not ultimately submitted to the FDA.

title: Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals Inc. v. Thompson
Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith, Inc. v. Dabit
summary: The Court unanimously ruled that SLUSA barred state law securities fraud class action "holder" claims, based on losses from retaining stock due to fraud, even though federal securities laws gave a private cause of action only to purchasers or sellers.

title: Metropolitan Edison Co. v. People Against Nuclear Energy
Meyer v. Holley
summary: The Court unanimously held that the Fair Housing Act imposed liability without fault on a corporate employer under traditional agency principles, normally making the corporation vicariously liable but not its officers or owners.

title: Michigan Department of State Police v. Sitz
summary: The Court held that police sobriety checkpoints met the Fourth Amendment standard of reasonable search and seizure, and so were constitutional under the federal Constitution.

title: Michigan v. EPA
summary: The Court held that the EPA must consider costs, and that it interpreted the Clean Air Act unreasonably when it decided it did not need to consider costs in finding that regulation was "necessary and appropriate."

title: Michigan v. Jackson
summary: The Court held, in a case about the Sixth Amendment right to counsel in police interrogation, that once an accused claimed counsel at a plea hearing or other proceeding, a later waiver during police questioning was invalid unless the accused initiated the communication.

title: Microsoft Corp. v. i4i Ltd. Partnership
Microsoft Corp. v. United States
summary: In a dispute over whether a Stored Communications Act warrant could compel production of emails stored in Ireland, the Court held the case moot after the CLOUD Act and a new warrant, and vacated the Second Circuit's decision.

title: Miller Bros. Co. v. Maryland
summary: The Court ruled that a mail order reseller was not required to collect a use tax unless it had sufficient contact with the state.

title: Miller Music Corp. v. Charles N. Daniels, Inc.
Milliken v. Bradley
summary: In a case over desegregation busing across district lines among 53 metropolitan Detroit school districts, the Court held that districts were not responsible for cross-district desegregation unless each had deliberately engaged in segregation.

title: Minerva Surgical, Inc. v. Hologic, Inc.
Minnesota Board for Community Colleges v. Knight
Minnesota Voters Alliance v. Mansky
summary: The Court ruled that a century-old Minnesota law barring voters from wearing political clothing or items at polling places was overbroad, violated free speech rights under the First Amendment, and was therefore unconstitutional.

title: Miranda v. Arizona
summary: The Court ruled that police must warn a person in custody of their constitutional rights before interrogation, or the person's statements cannot be used as evidence against them at trial.

title: Missouri v. Jenkins
summary: The Court reversed a district court ruling that had required Missouri to correct intentional racial discrimination in Kansas City schools by funding salary increases and remedial education programs.

title: Mitchell v. United States (1999)
summary: The Court considered Fifth Amendment self-incrimination rights in federal sentencing and ruled that pleading guilty does not waive the privilege at sentencing, and that courts cannot draw an adverse inference from silence when finding facts affecting the sentence's severity.

title: Monasky v. Taglieri
summary: In a case under the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction, the Court held that a child's habitual residence is determined by the totality of the circumstances, not by categorical requirements such as a parental agreement.

title: Monroe v. Pape
summary: The Court considered federal civil rights law applied to constitutional violations by city employees and held that 42 U.S.C. § 1983 could be used to sue state officers who violated a plaintiff's constitutional rights.

title: Monsanto Co. v. Durnell
summary: In a dispute over whether state-law cancer warnings for Roundup could be required when the EPA had not identified the product as carcinogenic, the Court ruled for Monsanto, holding that Missouri law could not override the EPA's uniform labeling requirements.

title: Monsanto Co. v. Geertson Seed Farms
summary: The Court reversed the lower court's decision barring partial deregulation of Monsanto's genetically modified Roundup-ready alfalfa pending completion of an environmental impact statement, finding the district court abused its discretion in enjoining it.

title: Mont v. United States
summary: The Court ruled that a term of supervised release is paused, or tolled, by imprisonment for another offense, in a case where a prisoner on supervised release was later jailed on state-law charges.

title: Montana v. United States
summary: The Court held that Montana, not the United States in trust for the Crow Tribe, held title to the Big Horn Riverbed under the Equal Footing Doctrine, and that the Tribe could not regulate nonmember hunting and fishing on nonmember-owned fee-simple land within its reservation.

title: Moody v. NetChoice, LLC
summary: The Court vacated the lower-court decisions in challenges to Florida and Texas laws limiting online content moderation, because the courts had not fully assessed the laws under the First Amendment, and remanded the cases for further consideration.

title: Moore v. Harper
summary: In a dispute over North Carolina's legislature-drawn congressional districts, the Court ruled that the Elections Clause does not give state legislatures sole power over federal elections, rejecting the independent state legislature theory.

title: Moore v. Texas (2017)
summary: In a death penalty case involving intellectual disability, the Court held that contemporary clinical standards determine what counts as an intellectual disability, and that even milder forms may bar a death sentence under the Eighth Amendment.

title: Moragne v. States Marine Lines, Inc.
Morissette v. United States
summary: The Court reversed the conviction of a scrap collector who sold spent bomb casings from an Air Force range he thought abandoned, holding that a crime requires criminal intent.

title: Mt. Healthy City School District Board of Education v. Doyle
summary: In a suit by a fired teacher against his school district, the Court held that the district was primarily a local entity beyond the Eleventh Amendment's reach, and remanded the case for the district court to examine whether he would have been fired anyway.

title: Mullin v. Al Otro Lado
summary: The Court held that a non-citizen arrives in the United States under the Immigration and Nationality Act only upon crossing the border, so the Act neither entitles a non-citizen standing in Mexico to apply for asylum nor requires inspection by an immigration officer.

title: Murphy v. National Collegiate Athletic Association
summary: In a challenge by New Jersey to the federal Professional and Amateur Sports Protection Act, the Court reversed the lower courts, held that the law violated the anticommandeering principle, and declared the entire law unconstitutional.

title: Murray v. United States
summary: The Court ruled that when officers conduct an unlawful search followed by a lawful one, evidence seized in the second search is admissible if that search is genuinely independent of the earlier one.

title: Murthy v. Missouri
summary: The Court ruled that Missouri and Louisiana lacked standing to sue the federal government over alleged pressure on social media companies to censor content, because they failed to show a substantial risk of redressable injury traceable to government action.

title: Musacchio v. United States
summary: The Court unanimously held that when reviewing a claim of insufficient evidence for a criminal offense, an appellate court should assess the elements of the alleged crime rather than the elements described in the jury instructions.

title: NAACP v. Button
summary: The Court held that a federal district court's reservation of jurisdiction did not bar its review of a state court ruling, and it overturned Virginia's 1956 laws targeting the NAACP's litigation as violating the First and Fourteenth Amendments.

title: NAACP v. Claiborne Hardware Co.
summary: The Court ruled that a state's broad power to regulate economic activities does not include the power to prohibit peaceful advocacy of a politically motivated boycott.

title: Napue v. Illinois
summary: The Court held that a prosecutor's knowing use of false testimony in a criminal case violates the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment, even if it affects only the witness's credibility and not the defendant's guilt or innocence.

title: National Ass'n of Home Builders v. Defenders of Wildlife
summary: The Court held that Section 7 of the Endangered Species Act applies only to federal agency actions involving agency discretion or control, so the EPA did not need to apply additional criteria when evaluating a transfer of Clean Water Act pollution control jurisdiction.

title: National Collegiate Athletic Association v. Alston
summary: The Court unanimously affirmed lower court rulings that NCAA restrictions on non-cash, academic-related compensation for college athletes, such as computers and internships, violated antitrust law.

title: National Institute of Family and Life Advocates v. Becerra
summary: The Court ruled that California's FACT Act notices, required of crisis pregnancy centers, likely violated the First Amendment by targeting speakers rather than speech.

title: National Pork Producers Council v. Ross
National Rifle Association of America v. Vullo
summary: The Court unanimously ruled that if a former New York financial regulator attempted to coerce financial institutions to refrain from doing business with the NRA, that conduct would violate the First Amendment.

title: Nautilus, Inc. v. Biosig Instruments, Inc.
summary: The Court, addressing the requirement that a patent particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention, held unanimously that a patent fails it when its claims fail to inform those skilled in the art about the invention's scope with reasonable certainty.

title: Navarette v. California
summary: The Court held that a 911 call reporting a recklessly driving pickup truck was reliable, and that officers did not need to personally observe criminal activity before conducting a traffic stop based on it.

title: Negusie v. Holder
summary: The Court held that the Board of Immigration Appeals and the Fifth Circuit erred in an asylum case by presuming that an applicant's claimed coercion to participate in persecution was immaterial to whether the persecutor bar applies.

title: Nestlé USA, Inc. v. Doe
summary: In a suit by former child slave laborers under the Alien Tort Statute against two U.S. companies for aiding and abetting slavery in Ivory Coast, the Court held that the plaintiffs improperly sought extraterritorial application of the statute.

title: Nevada Department of Human Resources v. Hibbs
summary: The Court held that the Family and Medical Leave Act of 1993 was narrowly targeted at sex-based overgeneralization and was a valid exercise of congressional power under Section 5 of the Fourteenth Amendment.

title: New Jersey v. New York
summary: In a dispute between two states over jurisdiction of Ellis Island, which was expanded by federal land reclamation, the Court ruled that roughly 83% of the island was part of New Jersey rather than New York.

title: New Jersey v. T. L. O.
summary: In a case about a school official's search of a student's purse after she was caught smoking, the Court held that the Fourth Amendment applies in schools but requires only reasonable suspicion, and ruled the search constitutional.

title: New Prime Inc. v. Oliveira
summary: In a dispute over classifying workers hired as contractors under the Federal Arbitration Act's arbitration exceptions, the Court unanimously ruled that the exceptions, such as for interstate commerce workers like truck drivers, apply to contractors as to regular employees.

title: New Process Steel, L.P. v. NLRB
summary: The Court held that the National Labor Relations Board could not make decisions without at least three members on a panel.

title: New York City Board of Education v. Tom F.
summary: In a dispute under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act over tuition reimbursement, the Court ruled in favor of the student, affirming the appellate court's decision by an evenly divided 4–4 vote.

title: New York State Department of Social Services v. Dublino
New York Times Co. v. Tasini
summary: The Court held that a newspaper publisher, in licensing back issues for electronic databases such as LexisNexis, could not license the works of freelance journalists contained in those newspapers, affirming the writers' copyright privileges.

title: New York Times Co. v. United States
summary: The Court ruled that the First Amendment protected the right of The New York Times to print the classified Pentagon Papers, despite the executive branch's claimed need for secrecy and the President's effort to stop publication.

title: New York v. Ferber
summary: The Court unanimously ruled that the First Amendment did not protect the sale or manufacture of child sexual abuse material, also known as child pornography, and that states could outlaw it.

title: New York v. Harris
summary: The Court ruled that a confession given at the police station was admissible, even though the suspect had been arrested illegally in his home without a warrant, because it was made outside the home after Miranda warnings.

title: New York v. O'Neill
summary: The Court held that a Florida statute enacting the Uniform Law to Secure the Attendance of Witnesses, letting courts in two states agree to subpoena a witness, did not on its face violate the Privileges and Immunities or Due Process Clauses.

title: Newman v. Piggie Park Enterprises, Inc.
Niemotko v. Maryland
summary: The Court held that a Maryland city violated the free exercise of religion by refusing a permit for Jehovah's Witnesses to meet in a public park when other religious and civic groups had received permits.

title: Nix v. Williams
summary: In a case about the exclusionary rule for evidence gathered through Fourth Amendment violations, the Court ruled that evidence law enforcement would inevitably have discovered through legal means remained admissible.

title: NLRB v. Gissel Packing Co.
summary: In a dispute over union authorization cards under the National Labor Relations Act, the Court upheld the NLRB's authority to order an employer that committed unfair labor practices to recognize and bargain with a union based solely on majority authorization cards.

title: NLRB v. Kentucky River Community Care, Inc.
Nordlinger v. Hahn
summary: The Court upheld Proposition 13, California's constitutional amendment that capped property taxes and limited reassessments to when property changes ownership.

title: Norfolk Shipbuilding & Drydock Corp. v. Garris
Norfolk Southern Railway Co. v. James N. Kirby, Pty Ltd.
NVIDIA v. E. Ohman J:or Fonder AB
O'Connor v. Ortega
summary: The Court, in a case over a search of a state hospital doctor's office during a workplace misconduct investigation, ruled that public employees retain their Fourth Amendment rights.

title: O'Connor-Ratcliff v. Garnier
summary: In a dispute over individuals blocked from a public official's personal social media account, the Court remanded the case to the Ninth Circuit for further consideration in light of a similar case decided the same day, Lindke v. Freed.

title: O'Hare Truck Service, Inc. v. City of Northlake
Ocasio v. United States
summary: The Court held that a conspiracy to violate the Hobbs Act can occur when an individual obtains property from another conspirator, in a case involving a police officer in a kickback scheme with an auto repair shop.

title: Octane Fitness, LLC v. ICON Health & Fitness, Inc.
Ohio Adjutant General's Department v. Federal Labor Relations Authority
Ohio v. American Express Co.
summary: In a dispute over credit card anti-steering provisions that barred merchants from steering customers to cards with lower fees, the Court affirmed the Appeals Court's ruling that the provisions did not violate antitrust laws.

title: Ohralik v. Ohio State Bar Ass'n
Oklahoma Statewide Charter School Board v. Drummond
Oklahoma Tax Commission v. Citizen Band, Potawatomi Indian Tribe of Oklahoma
summary: The Court held that an Indian tribe was not subject to state sales taxes on sales made to tribal members but was liable for state taxes on sales to non-tribal members.

title: Oklahoma v. Castro-Huerta
summary: The Court ruled that federal and state authorities held joint jurisdiction to prosecute non-Native Americans for crimes committed on Native American lands in Oklahoma, following the aftermath of McGirt.

title: Old Chief v. United States
summary: The Court concluded that Federal Rule of Evidence 403 required the trial court to accept a defendant's stipulation to a prior conviction, an element of the charged crime, over the prosecution's objection.

title: Olmstead v. L.C.
summary: The Court held that under the Americans with Disabilities Act, people with mental disabilities have the right to live in the community rather than institutions if professionals deem it appropriate, they do not oppose it, and it can be reasonably accommodated.

title: Opati v. Republic of Sudan
summary: The Court ruled unanimously that plaintiffs, including victims of the 1998 embassy bombings and their families, could seek punitive damages from foreign nations under the amended Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act for conduct preceding the amendment.

title: Oregon v. Ice
summary: In a case over sentencing for multiple offenses, the Court held that the Sixth Amendment does not prevent states from having judges, rather than juries, find the facts needed to impose consecutive rather than concurrent sentences.

title: Oregon Waste Systems, Inc. v. Department of Environmental Quality of Oregon
Orr v. Orr
summary: The Court held that Alabama statutes imposing alimony obligations on husbands but not on wives violated the equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

title: Osborne v. Ohio
summary: The Court held that the First Amendment allows states to outlaw possessing child pornography, not just distributing it, found Ohio's law not overbroad given a narrowing interpretation, and ordered a new trial.

title: Our Lady of Guadalupe School v. Morrissey-Berru
summary: The Court reversed the Ninth Circuit, ruling that under Hosanna-Tabor a person serving an important religious function, even without a religious leader's title or training, falls within the ministerial exception to employment discrimination laws.

title: Owasso Independent School District v. Falvo
Pacific Gas & Electric Co. v. Public Utilities Commission
summary: In a dispute over a utility's billing-envelope newsletters, the Court held that a state commission order forcing the utility to carry a rival group's message was unconstitutional, since the right to speak includes the right not to carry messages one disagrees with.

title: Pacific Gas & Electric Co. v. State Energy Resources Conservation & Development Commission
summary: The Court held that a state statute regulating economic aspects of nuclear generating plants was not preempted by the federal Atomic Energy Act of 1954.

title: Palmore v. Sidoti
summary: The Court rejected the consideration of racial bias in child custody proceedings, holding it unconstitutional under the 14th Amendment.

title: Panetti v. Quarterman
summary: The Court ruled that death-sentenced defendants may not be executed if they do not understand the reason for their imminent execution, and that once an execution date is set they may litigate their competency in habeas corpus proceedings.

title: Papachristou v. City of Jacksonville
summary: The Court declared a Jacksonville vagrancy ordinance unconstitutionally vague.

title: Parents Involved in Community Schools v. Seattle School District No. 1
summary: The Court found it unconstitutional for a school district to use race as a factor in assigning students to schools to match the district's overall racial composition, unless it was remedying a prior history of de jure segregation.

title: Parham v. Hughes
summary: The Court upheld a Georgia law that barred fathers of illegitimate children from bringing wrongful death claims without imposing the same burden on mothers.

title: Parisi v. Davidson
summary: The Court overturned the lower courts' decision to defer a soldier's habeas corpus petition seeking discharge as a conscientious objector until his court-martial ended, freeing the District Court to consider the petition.

title: Park 'N Fly
summary: In a dispute over an off-airport parking company's registered trademark, the Court affirmed the registration as more than a descriptive trademark.

title: Parker v. North Carolina
summary: The Court ruled that a plea agreement was valid even if the defendant entered it to avoid the death penalty and based on a possibly mistaken belief that his confession would be admissible in court.

title: Patchak v. Zinke
summary: The Court upheld a federal act that barred federal courts from hearing lawsuits involving a particular parcel of land, with a plurality holding that it did not violate Article III.

title: Payton v. New York
summary: The Court struck down a New York statute allowing warrantless entry into a private home to make a felony arrest, because the Fourth Amendment draws a firm line at the house's entrance absent exigent circumstances.

title: PennEast Pipeline Co. v. New Jersey
summary: In a case over state sovereign immunity and eminent domain powers delegated to private companies for a natural gas pipeline right-of-way, the Court ruled that states gave up their sovereign immunity from such delegated federal authority by ratifying the Constitution.

title: Pennsylvania v. Muniz
summary: The Court held that, of several incriminating statements a drunk-driving suspect made in police custody, only his confused answer about when he turned six was inadmissible, as it was testimonial; the others were admissible.

title: Pennsylvania v. Nelson
summary: The Court ruled that the federal Smith Act superseded the Pennsylvania Sedition Act, even though the state law came first, in a case where a man was convicted of sedition under the state law.

title: Penry v. Johnson
summary: The Court reversed the Texas courts in a case about whether sentencing instructions given to a Texas jury adequately emphasized mitigating factors for intellectually disabled defendants, finding the instructions insufficient.

title: Pepper v. United States
summary: The Court considered whether a district court properly handled the sentencing of a former methamphetamine dealer whose sentence was raised to 65 months after remands, and it ruled in favor of the defendant.

title: Percoco v. United States
summary: In a case about the federal honest services fraud statute, the Court held that a private citizen with significant influence over government decision-making cannot be convicted of honest services fraud for actions taken while not holding public office.

title: Pereida v. Wilkinson
summary: The Court ruled that a non-citizen seeking cancellation of a removal order did not meet the burden of proving eligibility unless they showed a past conviction was not disqualifying, even when the record was ambiguous under a divisible state statute.

title: Pereira v. Sessions
summary: In an immigration case, the Court reversed the lower court, holding that a Notice to Appear that does not tell a noncitizen when and where to appear for removal proceedings is not valid and does not trigger the stop-time rule.

title: Peretz v. United States
summary: In a federal felony trial where a magistrate judge supervised jury selection, the Court ruled that a defendant must affirmatively object, and that merely acquiescing to the magistrate's involvement is not enough to reverse a conviction.

title: Permanent Mission of India v. City of New York
Perpich v. Department of Defense
summary: In a case under the Militia Clauses of Article I, Section 8, the Court held that Congress may authorize National Guard members to be ordered to active federal duty for training abroad without the governor's consent or a declared national emergency.

title: Peugh v. United States
summary: The Court held that the Ex Post Facto Clause is violated when a defendant is sentenced under a later version of the Federal Sentencing Guidelines that provides a higher sentencing range than the version in place at the time of the offense.

title: Pfizer Inc. v. Government of India
summary: The Court held that foreign states could sue for treble damages in U.S. courts, because they should be recognized as "persons" under the Clayton Act.

title: PGA Tour, Inc. v. Martin
summary: The Court ruled for a golfer whose circulatory condition impaired his ability to walk, who sued the PGA Tour under the ADA to be allowed to use a golf cart in its qualifying tournament despite its walking requirement.

title: Philip Morris USA Inc. v. Williams
summary: The Court held that the due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment limits punitive damages, and it ordered a lower court to reconsider its damages awards on that basis.

title: Planned Parenthood of Central Missouri v. Danforth
summary: The Court upheld the right to have an abortion in a challenge to a Missouri abortion statute, declaring unconstitutional its requirement of prior written consent from a parent for a minor or a spouse for a married woman.

title: Plumhoff v. Rickard
summary: The Court held that it had jurisdiction and that police officers who fired shots at a driver during a high-speed car chase did not violate the Fourth Amendment's prohibition on unreasonable searches and seizures.

title: Polar Tankers, Inc. v. City of Valdez
Police Department of Chicago v. Mosley
summary: The Court ruled that a Chicago ordinance barring sidewalk protests near a school was a content-based restriction, since it treated labor-related protests differently, and held it unconstitutional for failing the higher standards for such restrictions.

title: Postal Service v. Council of Greenburgh Civic Ass'ns
summary: The Court upheld the constitutionality of a statute that prohibited depositing unstamped "mailable matter" in a mailbox approved by the United States Postal Service.

title: Poulos v. New Hampshire
summary: The Court held that a New Hampshire city ordinance on permission to hold meetings in a public park did not violate the appellant's free exercise rights, even if his group was arbitrarily and unlawfully denied a license for a religious meeting.

title: Powerex Corp. v. Reliant Energy Services Inc.
Powers v. Ohio
summary: The Court re-examined the Batson Challenge against race-based peremptory strikes and expanded it, allowing defendants and other parties to question peremptory challenges in jury selection regardless of race, under the Equal Protection Clause.

title: Price Waterhouse v. Hopkins
summary: An accounting firm denied an employee partnership allegedly because she did not fit the partners' idea of how a woman should look and act, and the Court held that this constituted sex discrimination under Title VII since the employer failed to prove it would have denied her anyway.

title: Priebe and Sons, Inc. v. United States
Prima Paint Corp. v. Flood & Conklin Manufacturing Co.
Pruneyard Shopping Center v. Robins
summary: The Court affirmed the California Supreme Court's decision in a free speech dispute between a shopping center and several local high school students who wished to canvass signatures for a petition against a U.N. General Assembly resolution.

title: Public Citizen v. Department of Justice
PUD No. 1 of Jefferson County v. Washington Department of Ecology
summary: In a dispute over whether a state could impose minimum water flow requirements on a proposed hydropower dam under section 401 of the Clean Water Act, the Court ruled in favor of the state.

title: Puerto Rico v. Franklin California Tax-Free Trust
summary: The Court held that Chapters 9 and 11 of the Federal Bankruptcy Code preempted the corresponding sections of Puerto Rico's Public Corporation Debt Enforcement and Recovery Act, because states may not enact municipal bankruptcy laws and Puerto Rico is usually treated as a "state."

title: Puerto Rico v. Sanchez Valle
summary: The Court, in a criminal case asking whether Puerto Rico and the federal government are separate sovereigns under the Double Jeopardy Clause, affirmed that the Clause bars both from successively prosecuting the same person for the same conduct under equivalent criminal laws.

title: Pulley v. Harris
summary: The Court held that the Eighth Amendment does not require a state appellate court, as an invariable rule, to proportionally compare a death sentence with penalties in similar cases before affirming it, even if the prisoner requests it.

title: Quality King Distributors, Inc. v. L'anza Research International, Inc.
Quanta Computer, Inc. v. LG Electronics, Inc.
Rabe v. Washington
summary: The Court reversed a drive-in theater manager's obscenity conviction, holding that Washington citizens had no notice under the Sixth Amendment that the place where a film was shown was an element of the offense.

title: Radovich v. National Football League
summary: The Court ruled that professional football, unlike professional baseball, was subject to antitrust laws, declining to extend to football the exemption that baseball had received.

title: Ragsdale v. Wolverine World Wide, Inc.
Railway Express Agency, Inc. v. New York
Ramos v. Louisiana
summary: The Court ruled that the Sixth Amendment requires unanimous guilty verdicts in criminal trials, applied that requirement to the states, and overturned its earlier decisions in Apodaca v. Oregon and Johnson v. Louisiana.

title: Rankin v. McPherson
summary: The Court ruled that a government employee's extremely critical remark about the President, made on a matter of public interest by someone with no policymaking role and little public interaction, was protected by the First Amendment, though direct threats would not be.

title: Ransom v. FIA Card Services, N.A.
summary: In a dispute over the Chapter 13 bankruptcy means test, the Court ruled that the car-ownership cost allowance was available only to debtors who made loan or lease payments on a vehicle, affirming the Ninth Circuit.

title: Ray v. Blair
summary: The Court ruled that states may constitutionally allow parties to require presidential elector candidates to pledge to vote for the party's nominees, and that denying the position to candidates who refused the pledge did not breach their rights.

title: Red Lion Broadcasting Co. v. FCC
summary: The Court held that radio broadcasters had First Amendment free speech rights that the FCC could partially restrict to serve the public interest in equitable use of scarce frequencies, so the Fairness Doctrine was constitutional.

title: Redrup v. New York
summary: The Court overturned the conviction of a newsstand clerk who sold paperback sex novels, ruling that written materials neither sold to minors nor foisted on unwilling audiences were constitutionally protected.

title: Reed v. Town of Gilbert
summary: The Court held that a town's sign ordinance, which put stricter limits on signs advertising religious services than on political or ideological signs, imposed content-based restrictions that did not survive strict scrutiny.

title: Reeves v. Sanderson Plumbing Products, Inc.
Reno v. American Civil Liberties Union
summary: The Court unanimously ruled that the indecency provisions of the 1996 Communications Decency Act, which regulated materials distributed via the Internet, violated the First Amendment's guarantee of freedom of speech.

title: Rent-A-Center, West, Inc. v. Jackson
summary: The Court held that under the Federal Arbitration Act, when an arbitration agreement delegates enforceability questions to the arbitrator, a challenge to that specific agreement goes to the district court, but a challenge to the whole agreement goes to the arbitrator.

title: Republic of Argentina v. NML Capital, Ltd.
summary: The Court found that Argentina, after defaulting on its debt and losing a federal collection action, had no foreign sovereign immunity shielding its foreign assets from discovery.

title: Rhode Island v. Innis
summary: The Court, clarifying what counts as interrogation under Miranda, held that interrogation includes not just direct questioning but also its functional equivalent, meaning police words or actions reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response.

title: Ricci v. DeStefano
summary: In a dispute over a city's decision to discard firefighter promotion test results because no black candidates scored high enough, the Court held that ignoring the results violated Title VII because the city lacked a "strong basis in evidence."

title: Rice v. Cayetano
summary: In a challenge to Hawaii's voting rules, the Court ruled that the state could not restrict eligibility to vote in elections for the Board of Trustees of the Office of Hawaiian Affairs to persons of Native Hawaiian descent.

title: Richlin Security Service Co. v. Chertoff
summary: In a dispute over attorney's fees under the Equal Access to Justice Act, the Court held that a prevailing party may be reimbursed for paralegal services at prevailing market rates rather than at the cost to the law firm.

title: Richmond Newspapers, Inc. v. Virginia
summary: After a murder case ended in three mistrials and the judge closed the fourth trial to the public and press, the Court ruled the closure violated the First and Fourteenth Amendments, which implicitly guarantee the press access to public trials.

title: Rico v. United States
summary: In a case about the fugitive-tolling doctrine, the Court held that the Sentencing Reform Act does not authorize a rule automatically extending a defendant's supervised release term when the defendant fails to report to probation.

title: Rimini Street Inc. v. Oracle USA Inc.
summary: In a copyright infringement dispute, the Court held that the Copyright Act's award of "full costs" to a prevailing party was limited to the taxable costs defined by the Fee Act of 1853, rejecting a broader reading covering other litigation expenses.

title: Ritzen Group, Inc. v. Jackson Masonry, LLC
summary: In a bankruptcy case over a motion for relief from an automatic stay, the Court unanimously ruled that a bankruptcy court's unreserved grant or denial of relief is a final order that may be appealed, and it affirmed the court below.

title: Roberts v. United States Jaycees
summary: In a case about associative freedom and a Minnesota antidiscrimination law, the Court held that the Minneapolis branch of the United States Jaycees could not bar women from becoming voting members.

title: Robertson v. United States ex rel. Watson
Robinson v. California
summary: The Court struck down a California law that criminalized being addicted to narcotics, in a decision interpreting the Eighth Amendment to prohibit particular acts or conduct from being punished.

title: Robinson v. Florida
summary: The Court reversed the convictions of white and African American people refused restaurant service, holding that a Florida rule requiring separate lavatories for restaurants serving both races entangled the state in discrimination, violating the Equal Protection Clause.

title: Rockwell International Corp. v. United States
summary: The Court examined the original-source exception to the False Claims Act's public-disclosure bar and held that the original-source requirement is jurisdictional and that "information on which the allegations are based" refers to the relator's own allegations.

title: Rodríguez v. Popular Democratic Party
summary: The Court considered whether Puerto Rico could by statute give a political party the power to fill an interim vacancy in its Legislature, and it upheld the Puerto Rico Supreme Court's decision that this did not violate the Constitution.

title: Roe v. Wade
summary: The Court ruled that the Constitution protected the right of pregnant women to choose to have an abortion before the point of fetal viability, striking down many state abortion laws.

title: Rogers v. Bellei
summary: The Court held that a person born outside the United States who received citizenship at birth through an automatic congressional grant could lose it for failing to meet reasonable residence requirements Congress imposed as a condition subsequent.

title: Rogers v. Tennessee
summary: The Court held that there was no due process violation for lack of fair warning when courts broadened pre-existing common law limitations on what acts constitute a crime under a more broadly worded statute to include additional acts.

title: Romag Fasteners, Inc. v. Fossil, Inc.
summary: In a trademark case under the Lanham Act, the Court ruled that a plaintiff in an infringement lawsuit does not have to show the defendant willfully infringed in order to claim lost profit damages.

title: Rompilla v. Beard
summary: The Court held that a convicted murderer received ineffective assistance of counsel because his lawyer failed to adequately investigate evidence the prosecution would likely use, reversing the Third Circuit and overturning his death sentence.

title: Rosenbloom v. Metromedia, Inc.
summary: In a libel suit against a media company, the Court ruled that the actual malice standard applied to a private individual because the story was a matter of public concern, and that the evidence did not support the damages awarded.

title: Roth v. United States
summary: The Court, in a case on what counts as obscene material unprotected by the First Amendment, created a new test for obscenity, upheld the defendant's conviction and allowed some obscenity prosecutions, while drastically loosening obscenity laws.

title: Rowan v. United States Post Office Department
summary: The Court ruled that a recipient of postal mail has sole and unreviewable discretion to decide whether to receive further material from a sender, who has no constitutional right to send unwanted material into someone's home.

title: Rubin v. Islamic Republic of Iran
summary: The Court unanimously upheld the judgment that ancient Persian artifacts owned by Iran could not be seized by families of bombing victims, ruling that the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act exceptions did not apply.

title: Rucho v. Common Cause
summary: In a challenge to partisan gerrymandering in districting plans, the Court ruled that federal courts cannot review such claims because they present nonjusticiable political questions, even if the practice may be incompatible with democratic principles.

title: Rummel v. Estelle
summary: The Court upheld a life sentence with the possibility of parole under Texas' three strikes law for a felony fraud crime, where the offense and two prior offenses involved about $230 of fraudulent activity.

title: Rumsfeld v. Padilla
summary: In a case over a U.S. citizen's military detention as an "unlawful combatant," the Court did not decide the detention-authority issue and held that the habeas corpus petition had been improperly filed.

title: S. D. Warren Co. v. Maine Board of Environmental Protection
summary: In a dispute over Clean Water Act licensing requirements, the Court ruled unanimously that hydroelectric dams were subject to section 401, since the simple flowing of water from a dam qualified as a "discharge" under its ordinary meaning.

title: Sackett v. Environmental Protection Agency (2023)
summary: The Court held that the Clean Water Act covers only wetlands that have a "continuous surface connection" to "waters of the United States" connected to "traditional interstate navigable waters".

title: Saia v. New York
summary: The Court held that an ordinance banning sound amplification devices without the Chief of Police's permission was facially unconstitutional because it was a prior restraint on free speech in violation of the First Amendment.

title: Salazar v. Buono
summary: In a dispute over a Latin cross placed on a rock outcropping in the Mojave National Preserve to honor war dead, the Court ruled that the cross may stay but sent the case back to a lower court.

title: San Diego Building Trades Council v. Garmon
Santosky v. Kramer
summary: In a case over the burden of proof for terminating parental rights for permanent neglect, the Court reversed and vacated the lower ruling, holding that states must show at least clear and convincing evidence to sever parental rights irrevocably.

title: Scheidler v. National Organization for Women (2003)
Scheidler v. National Organization for Women (2006)
Schmerber v. California
summary: The Court held that forcibly extracting and analyzing a suspect's blood sample was not compelled testimony and so did not violate the Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination.

title: Schneckloth v. Bustamonte
summary: In a consent search case, the Court ruled that knowledge of the right to refuse consent is a factor in whether consent was voluntary, but the state does not need to prove the person knew of that right under the Fourth Amendment.

title: Schriro v. Landrigan
summary: The Court held that the District Court did not abuse its discretion in refusing an evidentiary hearing to a convicted murderer who had told his counsel not to present mitigation evidence at sentencing, reversing the Ninth Circuit's en banc ruling.

title: Schwab v. Reilly
summary: The Court held that when a debtor claims an exemption of a dollar value for specific property, claiming its full anticipated value did not exempt the property from seizure if its true value was greater, and the trustee did not need to object.

title: Scott v. Harris
summary: The Court ruled for the deputy in a qualified immunity and excessive force suit by a motorist paralyzed after being run off the road in a chase, finding his actions objectively reasonable because videotape showed the motorist endangered public safety.

title: Seila Law LLC v. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau
summary: The Court held that the structure of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, with a single director removable only "for cause," violated the constitutional separation of powers principle.

title: Seling v. Young
summary: The Court rejected a challenge to Washington state's civil commitment statute for sexual predators, following earlier cases that had upheld civil commitment statutes.

title: Sessions v. Morales-Santana
summary: The Court unanimously found that the Immigration and Nationality Act's longer physical presence requirements for unwed fathers than for unwed mothers, for conveying citizenship to a foreign-born child, violated equal protection and due process.

title: Seymour v. Superintendent of Washington State Penitentiary
Shady Grove Orthopedic Associates, P.A. v. Allstate Ins. Co.
summary: The Court held that a federal district court sitting in a state with competing rules must apply a Federal Rule of Civil Procedure if the Rule is "arguably procedural."

title: Sharp v. Murphy
summary: The Court, in a per curiam decision following McGirt v. Oklahoma, ruled that Congress never disestablished the Muscogee (Creek) Nation reservation, which remained Indian country for purposes of the Major Crimes Act.

title: Shaw v. Reno
summary: The Court ruled that redistricting based on race, here a snake-like majority-minority North Carolina district drawn solely on race, must meet strict scrutiny under the Equal Protection Clause and violated the Fourteenth Amendment.

title: Shearson/American Express Inc. v. McMahon
summary: In a dispute over mandatory arbitration of private securities fraud claims, the Court held that Wilko v. Swan did not apply to claims under the 1934 Act, reversing the Second Circuit, and also held that RICO claims were arbitrable.

title: Sheetz v. County of El Dorado
summary: In a dispute over land-use permit fees under the Takings Clause, the Court unanimously held that such fees must be closely related and roughly proportional to the land use's effects, even when set by legislation rather than individualized assessment.

title: Shelby County v. Holder
summary: In a challenge to provisions of the Voting Rights Act of 1965, the Court ruled that the Section 4(b) coverage formula was unconstitutional because it relied on data over 40 years old, though it did not strike down Section 5.

title: Sherbert v. Verner
summary: The Court held that the Free Exercise Clause required the government to show a compelling interest and narrow tailoring before denying unemployment compensation to a woman fired because her job conflicted with her religion.

title: Simon v. Eastern Kentucky Welfare Rights Organization
summary: The Court held that indigent individuals and organizations representing them lacked Article III standing to challenge an IRS revenue ruling giving favorable treatment to hospitals that limited non-emergency care for indigent patients.

title: Sinochem International Co. v. Malaysia International Shipping Corp.
Skinner v. Switzer
summary: In a dispute over whether a prisoner seeking biological DNA material for testing to challenge his conviction must use a civil rights suit or a habeas corpus petition, the Court held that the civil rights path was appropriate.

title: Smiley v. Citibank (South Dakota), N. A.
Smith v. Goguen
summary: The Court held that a Massachusetts flag desecration law prohibiting "publicly treat[ing] contemptuously the flag of the United States" was unconstitutionally void for vagueness.

title: Snyder v. Louisiana
summary: In a death penalty case about racial issues in jury selection, the Court ruled that the prosecutor's use of peremptory strikes to remove African American jurors violated its earlier holding in Batson v. Kentucky.

title: Societe Internationale Pour Participations Industrielles et Commerciales, S.A. v. Rogers
Solem v. Helm
summary: The Court overturned a mandatory sentence of life in prison without parole, given to a man with a seventh nonviolent felony conviction for writing a check from a fictitious account, as cruel and unusual punishment.

title: Solid Waste Agency of Northern Cook County v. Army Corps of Engineers
summary: The Court held that the Corps of Engineers' use of the "migratory bird rule" to extend Clean Water Act Section 404 permitting authority to isolated waters, including isolated wetlands, exceeded the authority granted by that section.

title: South Carolina v. Catawba Indian Tribe, Inc.
summary: In a land claim brought by a terminated tribe, the Court held that federal policy did not preclude applying a state statute of limitations to the claim, and it remanded to the Fourth Circuit to decide whether South Carolina's statute applied.

title: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc.
summary: The Court held that states may charge tax on purchases from out-of-state sellers even without a physical presence in the taxing state, overturning its earlier decision that had barred such collection requirements under the Dormant Commerce Clause.

title: Southern Union Co. v. United States
Southland Corp. v. Keating
summary: In a dispute where 7-Eleven franchisees sued in California state court and the parent company invoked arbitration clauses, the Court held that the Federal Arbitration Act applied to contracts executed under state law.

title: Speiser v. Randall
summary: The Court held that a loyalty oath requirement for a property tax exemption violated the procedural due process rights of applicants who refused to sign, because it put the burden of proving their speech was not criminal on them rather than the state.

title: Sprint/United Management Co. v. Mendelsohn
summary: In an individual age discrimination case, the Court held that the relevance of co-workers' "me too" evidence is fact based and depends on many factors, so reviewing courts may not apply per se rules of admissibility or inadmissibility.

title: St. Mary's Honor Center v. Hicks
Standard Oil Co. of New Jersey v. United States
summary: The Court ruled that a petroleum conglomerate had illegally monopolized the American petroleum industry and ordered it to break itself up, while holding that antitrust law bans only "unreasonable" restraints on trade.

title: Stanley v. City of Sanford
summary: The Court held that Title I of the Americans with Disabilities Act protects only qualified individuals who hold or desire a position, and affirmed dismissal of a retired firefighter's claim over reduced post-employment health benefits.

title: Stanley v. Georgia
summary: The Court unanimously overturned a conviction for possessing obscene films found in a man's home and invalidated state laws forbidding private possession of obscene materials on First and Fourteenth Amendment grounds.

title: Stansbury v. California
summary: The Court considered whether an officer's undisclosed opinion that a questioned person was a suspect mattered for Miranda custody, and held unanimously that such a subjective view was irrelevant, reversing and remanding.

title: Star Athletica, LLC v. Varsity Brands, Inc.
summary: In a dispute between two cheerleading uniform makers, the Court rejected the argument that the designs were uncopyrightable because of their utilitarian purpose and held that the aesthetic elements of the clothing designs could be copyrightable.

title: Staub v. Proctor Hospital
summary: The Court held that an employer may be liable for employment discrimination under USERRA if a biased supervisor's actions proximately caused an adverse employment action, even if the ultimate decision-maker was not personally biased.

title: Stern v. Marshall
summary: The Court held that a bankruptcy court, as a non-Article III court, lacked constitutional authority under Article III to enter a final judgment on a state law counterclaim not resolved in ruling on a creditor's proof of claim, despite Congress's statutory grant.

title: Stoner v. California
summary: The Court extended the situations in which search warrants are required and reversed a robbery conviction that rested on evidence from a hotel room searched with only the desk clerk's permission.

title: Strate v. A-1 Contractors
summary: In a case about tribal courts' authority over civil disputes between nonmembers on public highways in Indian Country, the Court held that, absent Congressional authorization, tribal courts could not adjudicate such matters on state-maintained highways crossing reservation land.

title: Street v. New York
summary: The Court held that a New York law criminalizing publicly mutilating, defacing, defiling, or casting contempt upon the U.S. flag by words or act was partly unconstitutional because it prohibited speech against the flag.

title: Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard
summary: The Court ruled that race-based affirmative action programs in most college admissions violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment, in a suit alleging Harvard's admissions discriminated against Asian Americans.

title: Sturgeon v. Frost
summary: In disputes over National Park Service authority in Alaska under ANILCA, the Court ruled the Service may regulate only "public" lands, and later unanimously held navigable waters are "non-public" lands exempt from its regulations.

title: Sullivan v. Zebley
summary: In a case about determining childhood Social Security disability benefits, the Court ruled that substantial parts of the SSI program's regulation on childhood disability were inconsistent with the Social Security Act's "comparable severity" standard.

title: Summers v. Earth Island Institute
summary: The Court rejected the environmental groups' argument that they still had standing to challenge the Forest Service's exemption process generally, after their dispute over salvage timber sales on 238 acres was settled.

title: Susan B. Anthony List v. Driehaus
Sweatt v. Painter
summary: A Black man was refused admission to a state law school because the state constitution prohibited integrated education, and the Court ruled in his favor, reasoning that the racially separate law school was in fact unequal.

title: T.M. v. University of Maryland Medical System Corp.
summary: In a case concerning the Rooker–Feldman doctrine, the Court held that the doctrine bars federal court review of state court decisions even if those decisions are subject to further review in state court.

title: Tahoe-Sierra Preservation Council, Inc. v. Tahoe Regional Planning Agency
Takahashi v. Fish & Game Commission
summary: In a challenge by Japanese-American fishermen to a California law barring "aliens ineligible to citizenship" from getting fishing licenses, the Court held the restriction unreasonable and discriminatory against residents of Japanese ancestry.

title: TC Heartland LLC v. Kraft Foods Group Brands LLC
summary: In a dispute over where patent infringement suits could be brought, the Court unanimously ruled for the petitioner, upholding its 1957 decision that patent infringement cases must be heard in the district where the defendant is incorporated.

title: Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Ass'n v. Brentwood Academy
summary: The Court held that a statewide association's rule prohibiting high-school football coaches from contacting middle-school prospects did not violate the First Amendment.

title: Tennessee v. Garner
summary: The Court held that under the Fourth Amendment, an officer pursuing a fleeing suspect may not use deadly force to prevent escape unless there is probable cause that the suspect poses a significant threat of death or serious physical injury.

title: Tennessee Valley Authority v. Hill
summary: In a challenge to the Tellico Dam's construction over the endangered snail darter, the Court ruled for the plaintiffs and upheld an injunction, finding the dam's operation would conflict with Section 7 of the Endangered Species Act.

title: Terminiello v. City of Chicago
summary: The Court held that a Chicago "breach of peace" ordinance banning speech that stirred the public to anger, invited dispute, brought about unrest, or created a disturbance was unconstitutional under the First and Fourteenth Amendments.

title: Terry v. United States
summary: The Court unanimously ruled that the First Step Act allows retroactive sentence reductions for pre-2010 drug-possession crimes, but only for those sentenced under minimum sentencing requirements.

title: Texas Department of Community Affairs v. Burdine
Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs v. Inclusive Communities Project, Inc.
summary: The Court held that disparate impact claims are cognizable under the Fair Housing Act, because Congress intended to include them, but that a plaintiff must prove the defendant's policies cause the disparity.

title: Texas Monthly, Inc. v. Bullock
summary: In a challenge to a Texas statute exempting religious publications from state sales tax, the Court overturned an appellate court's decision that the exemption was constitutional and remanded the case.

title: Texas v. New Jersey
summary: In a dispute among three states over which could escheat intangible personal property such as uncashed checks, the Court ruled that authority lay with the state of the creditor's last known address.

title: Textile Workers v. Darlington Manufacturing Co.
The Tidelands Case
summary: In a dispute over the three-mile marginal belt along California's coast, the Court held that California did not own it and that the Federal Government had paramount rights and full dominion over its resources, including oil.

title: Thermtron Products, Inc. v. Hermansdorfer
summary: The Court held that a federal district court may not decline jurisdiction over a properly removed state case because it is backlogged, and that such a refusal may be reviewed by a writ of mandamus.

title: Things Remembered, Inc. v. Petrarca
summary: The Court held that when a bankruptcy court remanded a removed action to state court because of a timely-raised removal defect or lack of subject-matter jurisdiction, the removal statute barred a court of appeals from reviewing the order.

title: Thole v. U.S. Bank
summary: The Court held that participants in a defined-benefit retirement plan, who were guaranteed a fixed monthly payment regardless of the plan's value or investment decisions, lacked Article III standing to sue the plan's fiduciaries under ERISA.

title: Thompson v. North American Stainless
summary: The Court held that Title VII of the Civil Rights Act protects a worker from retaliation when the worker's fiancé files a workplace grievance.

title: Thornburg v. Gingles
summary: The Court unanimously found that official discrimination and racial campaign appeals, combined with a multimember districting scheme, impaired black voters' ability to elect their candidates, invalidating North Carolina General Assembly districts.

title: Thornburgh v. American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists
Thryv, Inc. v. Click-To-Call Technologies, LP
Tibble v. Edison International
summary: The Court held that because a fiduciary has a continuing duty to monitor investments and remove imprudent ones, a plaintiff may claim a breach of the duty of prudence, and the claim is timely if filed within six years of the alleged breach.

title: TikTok, Inc. v. Garland
summary: In a challenge by ByteDance and TikTok to a law requiring divestment of foreign adversary controlled apps on First Amendment and other grounds, the Court ruled the law constitutional because it satisfied intermediate scrutiny given national security concerns.

title: Till v. SCS Credit Corp.
summary: In a Chapter 13 bankruptcy cramdown dispute over a loan's value, the Court, with no majority opinion, approved a 9.5 percent rate that adjusted the national average loan rate for the risk of non-payment.

title: Timbs v. Indiana
summary: The Court unanimously ruled that the Eighth Amendment's prohibition of excessive fines is incorporated under the Fourteenth Amendment and so applies to state and local governments.

title: Times Film Corp. v. City of Chicago
summary: In two cases involving limits on freedom of expression for motion pictures, the Court affirmed the right of local governments to engage in some form of censorship.

title: Tinker v. Des Moines Independent Community School District
TrafFix Devices, Inc. v. Marketing Displays, Inc.
summary: In a trademark dispute, the Court determined that a functional design could not be eligible for trademark protection and established a presumption that a patented design is inherently functional.

title: Train v. City of New York
Trammel v. United States
summary: In a case on spousal privilege in the law of evidence, the Court held that the witness-spouse alone has a privilege to refuse to testify adversely, and it upheld the petitioner's conviction based on his wife's testimony.

title: Trans World Airlines, Inc. v. Hardison
summary: The Court held that under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, an employer may discharge an employee who observes a seventh-day sabbath, and that the employee is not entitled to equal employment opportunity protection.

title: TransUnion LLC v. Ramirez
summary: In a class-action dispute over Article III standing against a private defendant, the Court ruled that only those who can show concrete harm have standing to seek damages in federal court.

title: Travelers Casualty & Surety Co. of America v. Pacific Gas & Electric Co.
Trevino v. Thaler
summary: The Court held that, because Texas procedures did not afford a meaningful opportunity to raise ineffective assistance of counsel claims on direct appeal, such claims first raised in a federal habeas petition were not barred by procedural default.

title: Trump v. Anderson
