summary: The Court unanimously held that states could not determine eligibility for federal office, including the presidency, under Section 3 of the Fourteenth Amendment, after Colorado's Supreme Court had rejected Trump's eligibility.

title: Trump v. CASA, Inc.
summary: The Court considered whether lower-court judges could issue universal injunctions blocking nationwide enforcement of policies, and ruled that such injunctions exceed judicial power unless necessary to give the formal plaintiff "complete relief".

title: Trump v. Cook
summary: In a dispute over President Trump's attempt to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook "for cause," the Court denied the government's application and held that Cook could remain in her job while the removal efforts were litigated.

title: Trump v. Hawaii
summary: The Court reversed the Ninth Circuit, ruling that challengers to the presidential travel restriction proclamation were unlikely to succeed on their INA or Establishment Clause claims, and vacated the injunction and remanded.

title: Trump v. Mazars USA, LLP
summary: The Court held that courts must consider separation of powers in disputes over congressional subpoenas for the president's personal information, set out four non-exhaustive factors, and vacated the lower court's decision for not properly weighing those concerns.

title: Trump v. New York
summary: The Court vacated the District Court's ruling that had blocked a presidential memo directing the Commerce Department to report estimated counts of illegal immigrants in each state for congressional apportionment purposes.

title: Trump v. Slaughter
summary: In a challenge to the president's firing of an FTC commissioner without cause, the Court held that the president had the power to remove independent agency heads at will, overturning Humphrey's Executor.

title: Trump v. United States (2024)
summary: The Court held that presidential immunity from criminal prosecution presumptively extends to all of a president's official acts, with absolute immunity for official acts within exclusive presidential authority that Congress cannot regulate.

title: TSC Industries, Inc. v. Northway, Inc.
Turner Broadcasting System, Inc. v. FCC
summary: In a dispute over FCC must-carry rules for cable television operators, the Court held in the first ruling that cable companies were First Amendment speakers, and in the second held the rules were not restrictions of their free speech rights.

title: Twitter, Inc. v. Taamneh
summary: The case asked whether internet service providers were liable for aiding and abetting a foreign terrorist organization by recommending user-posted content, and the Court unanimously ruled the charges against Twitter and other companies were not permissible under the Antiterrorism Act.

title: Tyler v. Cain
summary: The Court held that the rule from Cage v. Louisiana, which found certain jury instructions on reasonable doubt unconstitutional, was not made retroactive to cases on collateral review by the Supreme Court.

title: U.S. Term Limits, Inc. v. Thornton
summary: The Court ruled that states cannot impose qualifications for prospective members of Congress stricter than those the Constitution specifies, invalidating 23 states' congressional term limit provisions.

title: Union Pacific Railroad Co. v. Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers
summary: The Court held that, because nothing in the Railway Labor Act made the obligation to conference minor disputes or prove conferencing jurisdictional, the act's limited grounds for relief should not be treated as a constitutional due process issue.

title: United Automobile Workers v. Johnson Controls, Inc.
United Building & Construction Trades Council v. Mayor and Council of Camden
summary: The Court held that a city can pressure private employers to hire city residents, but using that power to bias private contractors against out-of-state residents may be challenged under the Privileges and Immunities Clause of Article Four.

title: United Gas Pipe Line Co. v. Memphis Light, Gas, & Water Division
United Haulers Ass'n v. Oneida-Herkimer Solid Waste Management Authority
summary: The Court held that New York county ordinances forcing private waste management companies to deliver waste to a public facility did not discriminate against interstate commerce.

title: United States ex rel. Knauff v. Shaughnessy
United States Forest Service v. Cowpasture River Preservation Ass'n
summary: In a dispute over a Forest Service permit for a pipeline under the Appalachian Trail, the Court ruled that the Trail's assignment to the NPS did not make its lands NPS lands, so the Forest Service could issue the permit.

title: United States National Bank of Oregon v. Independent Insurance Agents of America
United States Railroad Retirement Board v. Fritz
United States v. 12 200-ft. Reels of Film
summary: The Court held that the First Amendment did not require that citizens be allowed to import obscene material for their personal and private use at home.

title: United States v. Antelope
summary: The Court held that American Indians convicted on reservation land were not deprived of equal protection, because the federal criminal statutes rested on political membership in an Indian tribe or nation rather than on impermissible racial classifications.

title: United States v. Apel
summary: The Court held that, in deciding whether someone trespassed after being ordered to leave by a commanding officer, a "military installation" covers the commander's entire area of responsibility, including base areas the public may visit through easements.

title: United States v. Arthrex, Inc.
summary: In a dispute over the Appointments Clause and patent judges on the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, the Court ruled the judges were principal officers, but resolved the problem by making their decisions reviewable by the Director of the Patent Office.

title: United States v. Arvizu
summary: The Court unanimously reaffirmed that the Fourth Amendment required courts to judge the reasonableness of a traffic stop by the totality of the circumstances rather than examining each of an officer's reasons for the stop individually.

title: United States v. Bajakajian
summary: The Court held that asset forfeiture is unconstitutional under the Eighth Amendment's Excessive Fines Clause when it is grossly disproportional to the gravity of the defendant's offense, striking down the federal government's forfeiture.

title: United States v. Booker
summary: In a criminal sentencing case, the Court ruled that the Sixth Amendment requires that, apart from prior convictions, only facts admitted by the defendant or proved to a jury beyond a reasonable doubt may be used to calculate a sentence above the statutory maximum.

title: United States v. Briggs (2020)
summary: The Court ruled unanimously that under the Uniform Code of Military Justice, rapes committed between 1986 and 2006 that were "punishable by death" had no statute of limitations, unlike similar civilian crimes.

title: United States v. Continental Can Co.
United States v. Cook
summary: In a dispute over timber cut and sold from Indian reservation land, the Court held that the tribes did not own the land, only had a right to occupy it, and could not cut and sell timber merely to sell it.

title: United States v. Craft
summary: The Court held that a spouse in a tenancy by the entirety possesses an individual right in their own estate sufficient to constitute "rights to property" for the purpose of a lien.

title: United States v. DiFrancesco
summary: The Court held that a provision of the Organized Crime Control Act of 1970 letting the federal government appeal certain criminal sentences after they are imposed did not violate the Fifth Amendment's Double Jeopardy Clause.

title: United States v. Dixon
summary: In a double jeopardy case, the Court overruled an earlier decision, revived the traditional Blockburger standard, and held that subsequent convictions for offenses containing the same elements violated the Double Jeopardy Clause.

title: United States v. Dominguez Benitez
summary: The Court ruled that a federal criminal defendant who did not alert the district court to a possible Rule 11 violation must show on appeal that the violation affirmatively affected his rights to obtain reversal of his guilty plea conviction.

title: United States v. Drayton
summary: In a case over a drug interdiction search on a Greyhound bus, the Court held that officers need not advise passengers of their right to refuse consent, and that the search was reasonable because the passengers voluntarily consented.

title: United States v. Freed
summary: The Court held that the National Firearms Act's registration requirements did not violate the Fifth Amendment and that possessing an unregistered firearm did not require specific intent, so a buyer of unregistered hand grenades was criminally liable.

title: United States v. Glaxo Group Ltd.
summary: In a patent-antitrust case, the Court held that the Government may challenge a patent's validity when the patent is directly involved in an antitrust violation, and that mandatory selling and compulsory patent licensing at reasonable charges are recognized antitrust remedies.

title: United States v. Grubbs
summary: The Court ruled that anticipatory search warrants, issued in advance of a "triggering condition" that makes them executable, are constitutional under the Fourth Amendment and need not describe that condition on their face.

title: United States v. Haggar Apparel Co.
summary: In a dispute over a customs classification regulation, the Court held that Chevron deference was appropriate for regulations issued by Customs on behalf of the Treasury, and rejected the importer's argument that the regulation applied only to customs officers.

title: United States v. Hemani
summary: The Court held that using the federal law banning unlawful drug users from possessing firearms to criminalize gun possession by habitual users, without proof of active intoxication or dangerousness, violated the Second Amendment.

title: United States v. Huck Manufacturing Co.
summary: In a patent-license price-fixing case, the Court was evenly split and affirmed the lower court's decision without issuing an opinion, leaving the question inconclusive.

title: United States v. Interstate Commerce Commission
United States v. Jorn
summary: The Court held that where a trial judge abruptly declared a mistrial to keep a prosecution witness from incriminating himself, the Double Jeopardy Clause barred a second trial of the defendant.

title: United States v. Knotts
summary: The Court held that using a beeper to help officers follow a car on a single trip violated no legitimate expectation of privacy, so it was no search or seizure and needed no warrant under the Fourth Amendment.

title: United States v. Kozminski
summary: In a case over a family accused of enslaving two men on their farm, the Court held that the jury had been improperly instructed on the nature of involuntary servitude and remanded for a new trial.

title: United States v. Line Material Co.
summary: The Court held that patent cross-licenses between two competing manufacturers that fixed the prices of the licensed products, with one licensing others under similar price fixing, violated Sherman Act § 1, and that knowing licensees joined a hub-and-spoke conspiracy.

title: United States v. Mead Corp.
summary: The Court, addressing when Chevron deference should be applied, determined that it applies when Congress delegated authority to the agency generally to make rules carrying the force of law.

title: United States v. Montoya De Hernandez
United States v. Morrison
summary: The Court found unconstitutional parts of the Violence Against Women Act of 1994, which let victims of gender-motivated violence sue attackers in federal court, because they exceeded Congress's powers under the Commerce Clause and the Equal Protection Clause.

title: United States v. National City Lines, Inc.
United States v. O'Brien
summary: The Court ruled that a criminal prohibition against burning a draft card did not violate the First Amendment's free speech guarantee, finding the law justified by a significant government interest unrelated to suppressing speech.

title: United States v. Oakland Cannabis Buyers' Cooperative
summary: The Court rejected the common-law medical necessity defense to crimes under the federal Controlled Substances Act, regardless of their legal status under state laws, such as California's, that recognize a medical use for marijuana.

title: United States v. Paramount Pictures, Inc.
summary: The Court affirmed the district court's ruling that the film studios' distribution scheme, involving studio-owned theaters and exclusive dealing arrangements, violated United States antitrust law.

title: United States v. Parke, Davis & Co.
summary: The Court held that a company that went beyond the Colgate doctrine by taking affirmative steps to induce adherence to its suggested prices formed a price-fixing combination among competitors, violating § 1 of the Sherman Act.

title: United States v. Philadelphia National Bank
United States v. Robel
summary: The Court ruled that the government could not deprive people of constitutional rights, here freedom of association, even in the interests of national security.

title: United States v. Rodriquez
summary: In a case interpreting the Armed Career Criminal Act, the Court ruled that although a crime's elements may not be considered "serious," sentence enhancements related to a defendant's prior record bear on how that determination is made.

title: United States v. Salvucci
summary: The Court ruled that "automatic standing" to bring a Fourth Amendment claim based merely on possession of a seized item lacks constitutional merit.

title: United States v. Seeger
summary: The Court ruled that the military draft exemption for conscientious objectors covered not only those who believed in a supreme being but also those whose sincere and meaningful beliefs held a place in their lives parallel to that of God.

title: United States v. Sineneng-Smith
summary: The Court unanimously vacated the Ninth Circuit's decision striking down the law criminalizing encouraging illegal immigration, because the panel violated the party presentation principle by raising overbreadth itself, and remanded for reconsideration.

title: United States v. Sioux Nation of Indians
summary: The Court held that Congress did not violate separation of powers by letting the Sioux Nation pursue a previously adjudicated claim, and that taking the Black Hills land set aside for the tribe required just compensation, including interest.

title: United States v. Sisson
summary: In a Selective Service case where the judge ordered an acquittal after a jury returned a guilty verdict, the Court held that the government had no power to appeal an acquittal, however wrong its legal basis.

title: United States v. Southwestern Cable Co.
United States v. Texas (2016)
summary: In a challenge to the constitutionality of the Deferred Action for Parents of Americans program, the Court, equally divided, affirmed the lower-court injunction blocking President Obama's program.

title: United States v. Texas (2021)
summary: The case concerned whether the federal government could sue Texas to stop enforcement of its six-week abortion ban, and the Court ruled per curiam that certiorari was improvidently granted and dismissed the case.

title: United States v. Texas (2023)
summary: The Court held that Texas and Louisiana lacked Article III standing to challenge a Biden administration immigration policy that prioritized apprehending and deporting suspected terrorists, non-citizens who committed crimes, and those recently caught at the border.

title: United States v. Thompson-Center Arms Co.
United States v. United States Gypsum Co.
summary: The Court held that a patent licensing program that fixed prices of many licensees and regimented an entire industry violated the antitrust laws, and later held that relief did not let compulsory-license licensees challenge the patents' validity.

title: United States v. Vaello Madero
summary: In a case over excluding U.S. citizens in Puerto Rico from Supplemental Security Income, the Court ruled that Congress's broad power over the territories under Article Four meant the exclusion did not violate the Fifth Amendment's Due Process Clause.

title: United States v. White Mountain Apache Tribe
summary: In a dispute over deteriorated Fort Apache buildings held in trust for an Indian tribe, the Court affirmed the appellate court, holding that the federal government used the trust property and therefore had a duty to maintain it.

title: United States v. X-Citement Video, Inc.
summary: The Court reversed the Ninth Circuit, which had found federal child pornography laws unconstitutionally vague, because the relevant sections could be interpreted in a constitutional way.

title: United States v. Zubaydah
summary: In a dispute over the state secrets privilege, where an alleged Al Qaeda operative sought testimony from CIA contractors about his torture at a black site and the government blocked it as classified, the Court ruled against him.

title: Universal Health Services, Inc. v. United States ex rel. Escobar
summary: The Court held that the implied false certification theory can be a basis for False Claims Act liability when a claim makes specific representations but fails to disclose noncompliance with material requirements that make them misleading.

title: US Airways, Inc. v. Barnett
summary: In a case about reasonable accommodations under the Americans with Disabilities Act, the Court held that a requested accommodation such as a transfer can be unreasonable if it would violate the employer's seniority system.

title: USAID v. Alliance for Open Society International (2013)
summary: The Court ruled that conditions imposed on recipients of certain federal grants restricted freedom of speech and violated the First Amendment.

title: Utah v. Strieff
summary: The Court limited the scope of the Fourth Amendment's exclusionary rule.

title: Utility Air Regulatory Group v. EPA
summary: In a case about the EPA's regulation of air pollution under the Clean Air Act, the Court, in a divided decision, largely upheld the EPA's ability to regulate greenhouse emissions.

title: Uzuegbunam v. Preczewski
summary: The Court held that in a case about nominal damages for suppressed free speech rights later mooted by intervening circumstances, nominal damages for a past rights violation satisfy Article III's redressability requirement.

title: Vacco v. Quill
summary: The Court ruled that New York's ban on physician-assisted suicide was constitutional, holding that preventing doctors from assisting even terminally ill or suffering patients was a legitimate state interest within the state's authority.

title: Vaden v. Discover Bank
summary: The Court held that a federal court may look at the underlying controversy of a Federal Arbitration Act §4 petition to decide whether it "arises under" federal law, but that controversy must satisfy the well-pleaded complaint rule for jurisdiction.

title: Van Buren v. United States
summary: In a case over the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act's definition of "exceeds authorized access," the Court ruled that one exceeds authorized access by accessing off-limit files and information on a computer system they were otherwise authorized to access.

title: Van Orden v. Perry
summary: The Court ruled that a display of the Ten Commandments on a monument given to the government at the Texas State Capitol did not violate the Establishment Clause, holding the display constitutional.

title: Verizon Communications Inc. v. Law Offices of Curtis V. Trinko, LLP
summary: The Court held that the Telecommunications Act of 1996 had not modified the Sherman Act's framework, preserving claims meeting established antitrust standards without creating new ones, and it refused to extend the essential facilities doctrine.

title: Vermont v. Brillon
summary: The Court held that trial delay caused by a criminal defendant's public defender should be attributed to the defense rather than the government, and so did not violate the Speedy Trial Clause of the Sixth Amendment.

title: Vernonia School District 47J v. Acton
summary: The Court upheld a public school district's random drug testing of student-athletes, holding that although the tests were Fourth Amendment searches, they were reasonable given the schools' interest in preventing teenage drug use.

title: Vieth v. Jubelirer
summary: The Court, in a plurality opinion, upheld the District Court's ruling for the appellees that the alleged political gerrymandering in the redistricting was not unconstitutional.

title: Viking River Cruises, Inc. v. Moriana
Virginia House of Delegates v. Bethune-Hill
Virginia Uranium, Inc. v. Warren
summary: The Court held that Virginia's ban on uranium mining did not conflict with the Atomic Energy Act, and it let the ban stand.

title: Waddington v. Sarausad
summary: The Court considered a driver's second-degree murder conviction for a gang-related shooting involving high school students and held that he was tried with due process and should not have been granted federal habeas corpus relief.

title: Wainwright v. Sykes
summary: The Court held that a state prisoner who failed to raise a federal constitutional claim at trial or on appeal as state rules required, without showing cause and prejudice, could not raise it later in federal habeas corpus proceedings.

title: Walker v. Armco Steel Corp.
summary: In a diversity action asking whether state law or Federal Rule 3 determined when an action commenced for tolling the state statute of limitations, the Court found no conflict because not applying the federal rule would not thwart its purpose.

title: Wallace v. Kato
summary: In a §1983 suit seeking damages for a false arrest followed by criminal proceedings, the Court held that the statute of limitations begins to run when the claimant is detained pursuant to legal process, not when the charges are dropped.

title: Wards Cove Packing Co. v. Atonio
Warner-Jenkinson Co. v. Hilton Davis Chemical Co.
Washington v. Glucksberg
summary: The Court unanimously held that a right to assisted suicide was not protected by the Due Process Clause.

title: Watchtower Bible & Tract Society of New York, Inc. v. Village of Stratton
summary: The Court held that a town ordinance making it a misdemeanor to engage in door-to-door advocacy without first registering with town officials and getting a permit violated the First Amendment as applied to religious proselytizing, anonymous political speech, and handbill distribution.

title: Waters v. Churchill
summary: The Court held that a public hospital did not need to determine what a nurse actually said in criticizing a supervisor's staffing practices, if it reasonably believed what she said and reasonably believed it could be disruptive, and it vacated the appeals court ruling.

title: Watson v. Employers Liability Assurance Corp.
Watson v. United States
summary: The Court held that a person who receives a firearm in exchange for drugs does not "use" a firearm during and in relation to a drug trafficking crime under the federal statute, unlike one who gives a gun for drugs.

title: Watters v. Wachovia Bank, N.A.
summary: The Court held that a nationally chartered bank's mortgage business, whether conducted by the bank or its operating subsidiary, is subject to the Comptroller of the Currency's superintendence rather than to state licensing, reporting, and visitorial regimes.

title: Weinberger v. Wiesenfeld
summary: The Court unanimously held that a Social Security Act provision letting widows but not widowers collect special benefits while caring for minor children violated the equal protection right secured by the Fifth Amendment's Due Process Clause.

title: Wesberry v. Sanders
summary: The Court ruled that U.S. House districts must be approximately equal in population, in a challenge to the unequal population of congressional districts in Georgia.

title: West Lynn Creamery, Inc. v. Healy
West Virginia v. EPA
summary: In a dispute over the EPA's Clean Air Act authority to regulate carbon emissions from existing power plants, the Court ruled that Congress did not authorize the EPA to require generation shifting without considering costs, which would have invalidated the Clean Power Plan.

title: Western Air Lines, Inc. v. Criswell
Westside Community Board of Education v. Mergens
Weyerhaeuser Company v. United States Fish and Wildlife Service
summary: The Court, in a unanimous decision, vacated the 5th Circuit's ruling that upheld the designation of private land in Louisiana as critical habitat for the dusky gopher frog and sent the case back for further review.

title: Whalen v. Roe
summary: In a challenge to a New York law requiring reporting and storage of Schedule II drug prescription information, the Court reversed the district court's decision that had held the statutes unconstitutional.

title: White v. Woodall
summary: The Court held that rejecting the requested jury instruction was not objectively unreasonable or contrary to clearly established law, so the defendant did not meet the requirements for habeas relief under AEDPA.

title: Whitmore v. Arkansas
summary: The Court held that the Eighth and Fourteenth Amendments do not require mandatory appellate review of death penalty cases, and that next-friend suits require a prior relationship and an appellant unable to litigate his own cause.

title: Whole Woman's Health v. Jackson
summary: In a challenge to a Texas law banning abortions after six weeks and enforced by private lawsuits, the Court ruled providers could not sue state-court judges, clerks, or the Attorney General, but their claims against state licensing officials could proceed.

title: Wilkie v. Robbins
summary: In a case on the scope of qualified immunity for Bureau of Land Management officials, the Court held that BLM employees could not be liable for an alleged retaliation claim by a farm owner because other avenues for relief were available.

title: Wilkins v. United States
summary: In a dispute over public use of an easement road near private properties, the Court reversed and remanded, holding that the Quiet Title Act's 12-year statute of limitations is a non-jurisdictional claims-processing rule.

title: Wilkinson v. United States
summary: The Court sustained the conviction of a housing administrator who refused to tell a congressional subcommittee whether he was a Communist Party member, upholding the conviction under the statute criminalizing refusal to answer pertinent questions from Congress.

title: Williams & Wilkins Co. v. United States
summary: The Court of Claims, later affirmed by an evenly divided Supreme Court, held that it was a fair use for libraries to photocopy articles for patrons engaged in scientific research.

title: Williams-Yulee v. Florida Bar
summary: The Court held that the First Amendment did not prohibit states from barring judges and judicial candidates from personally soliciting campaign funds, because the restriction was narrowly tailored to serve the compelling interest of keeping the judiciary impartial.

title: Williamson County Regional Planning Commission v. Hamilton Bank of Johnson City
Wilson v. Omaha Tribe
summary: In a land dispute, the Court held that 25 U.S.C. § 194 applied only to individuals and not to a state, that federal law governed the tribe's right to possession, and that state law determined how that applied to the natural movement of a river's boundaries.

title: Winkelman v. Parma City School District
Winston v. Lee
summary: The Court held that compelled surgical intrusion into a person's body to obtain evidence implicates privacy and security expectations so greatly that it would be unreasonable under the Fourth Amendment, even if it would likely produce evidence of a crime.

title: Winter v. Natural Resources Defense Council
Winters v. New York
summary: The Court ruled that a New York Penal Law section banning publication of periodicals dealing in criminal deeds was applied so vaguely that it violated the First Amendment, as applied through the Fourteenth.

title: Wis. Right to Life, Inc. v. FEC
Wisconsin Department of Revenue v. William Wrigley Jr. Co.
Witherspoon v. Illinois
summary: The Court ruled that a state statute giving the state unlimited challenges for cause against jurors who might have any objection to the death penalty violated the constitutional right to an impartial jury.

title: Woodford v. Ngo
summary: In a case about when prison litigation may be commenced in federal court, the Court ruled that prisoners must exhaust all state-court remedies in accordance with the rules thereof before filing claims in federal court.

title: Wygant v. Jackson Board of Education
Wyoming v. Houghton
summary: The Court held that, absent exigency, a warrantless search of a passenger's container capable of holding the object of a search supported by probable cause did not violate the Fourth Amendment, being justified under the automobile exception.

title: Ybarra v. Illinois
summary: The Court ruled that a warrant could not be used to search an unnamed individual unless the warrant mentioned that unnamed parties were involved or exigent circumstances were shown to exist.

title: Yeager v. United States
summary: The Court held that, even when a jury's acquittals on some counts seem inconsistent with its failure to return a verdict on other counts, the Double Jeopardy Clause bars the government from relitigating facts necessarily decided by the acquittals.

title: Young v. United Parcel Service
summary: In a case on disparate treatment claims under the Pregnancy Discrimination Act, the Court held that a pregnant employee must show the employer refused accommodations but later provided them to other employees with similar restrictions, and remanded.

title: Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer
summary: The Court limited the president's power to seize private property in a case arising when President Truman seized steel production facilities during the Korean War to head off a strike.

title: Zablocki v. Redhail
summary: The Court held that Wisconsin statutes requiring noncustodial parents to obtain a court order before receiving a marriage license violated the Fourteenth Amendment's Equal Protection Clause.

title: Zedner v. United States
summary: In a case about the right to a speedy trial, the Court unanimously ruled that a defendant cannot prospectively waive the protections of the Speedy Trial Act.

title: Zemel v. Rusk
summary: The Court held that the Secretary of State was statutorily authorized to refuse to validate United States citizens' passports for travel to Cuba, and that this grant of authority was constitutionally permissible.

title: Zenith Radio Corp. v. Hazeltine Research, Inc.
ZF Automotive U.S., Inc. v. Luxshare, Ltd.
summary: The Court unanimously ruled that a private arbitral tribunal overseas is not a "foreign or international tribunal" under 28 U.S.C. § 1782(a), and also held the same for the investor-state arbitral tribunal in the companion case.

title: Zubik v. Burwell
summary: In a dispute over whether religious institutions other than churches should be exempt from the ACA contraceptive mandate, the Court vacated the appeals court ruling and the six consolidated cases and sent them back to the courts of appeals for reconsideration.

title: Zuni Public School District No. 89 v. Department of Education
summary: The Court held that the statute authorizing the Federal Impact Aid Program permitted the Secretary of Education to identify districts to be disregarded by considering both the number of pupils and the size of expenditures per pupil.
